raw_summary: Autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. article_paragraphs: Autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie announced the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet , the company really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” says Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”

Greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial , as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of big battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

title: Scout Steps Toward Mass Production, With 200,000+ Reservations On The Line
raw_summary: Scout Motors, the revived American brand now focused on off-road capable and affordable electric trucks and SUVs, has apparently produced its first validation build vehicles at its factory in South Carolina. This is a significant step forward toward mass production for the Volkswagen Group subsidiary. We’ve seen many EV startups come and go, including ones that revived old, historic car brands — like Detroit Electric. However, in this case, Scout is 1) offering something unique on the market, 2) focused on affordability combined with usefulness, 3) backed by automotive giant Volkswagen Group, and 4) currently has more than 200,000 reservations on the books! Reportedly, there are 212,000+ reservations for Scout EVs.

This is a significant step forward toward mass production for the Volkswagen Group subsidiary.
article_paragraphs: Scout Motors, the revived American brand now focused on off-road capable and affordable electric trucks and SUVs, has apparently produced its first validation build vehicles at its factory in South Carolina. This is a significant step forward toward mass production for the Volkswagen Group subsidiary.

We’ve seen many EV startups come and go, including ones that revived old, historic car brands — like Detroit Electric. However, in this case, Scout is 1) offering something unique on the market, 2) focused on affordability combined with usefulness, 3) backed by automotive giant Volkswagen Group, and 4) currently has more than 200,000 reservations on the books! Reportedly, there are 212,000+ reservations for Scout EVs.

Oh, also, the company has a $2 billion factory in South Carolina, and it’s real. I’m sure there’s a lot to do there to get it filled out and operating as desired, but getting to factory production of validation build vehicles is a notable achievement that implies we are fairly close to getting actual production vehicles delivered to customers. The validation builds are of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup truck.
The company is now able to do stamping, welding, and painting at the factory in Blythewood, South Carolina, and CEO Scott Keogh says the factory is actually 85% complete already.

After validation builds, the next phase will be pre-production vehicles. Keogh forecasts that actual production of consumer cars will begin in 2027, and deliveries will then commence in 2028. (So, customer vehicle production must be slated for the end of next year.) Construction on the factory began in 2023.

Scout was initially only going to produce 100% electric vehicles. However, it pivoted to also producing extended-range electric vehicles (vehicles that always run on electricity from a battery but whose battery can be recharged from a gas engine while driving). According to the company, 87% of those 212,000+ reservations are for the range-extended versions of the Traveler and Terra. Buyers are also heavily favoring the SUV, the Traveler, which has pulled in 75% of the reservations so far.

Keogh thinks the company could reach 400,000 reservations by the time it starts producing customer vehicles. It was at 160,000 in March and 50,000 in January. The factory is supposed to have an annual production capacity of 200,000. Having reservations for two years worth of production would be a strong, helpful boost for the company.

All of that said, one warning on the reservation tally is it has one of the same issues as the Tesla Cybertruck had — reservations are fully refundable and only cost $100. That makes it very hard to know how many people will actually go ahead and buy the vehicles once they are on offer. We will see.

title: Your Car's D3 Gear Has A Purpose, And Here's What It Does
raw_summary: We've all heard of P, R, N, D, and L, but what about D3? article_paragraphs: We've all heard of P, R, N, D, and L, but what about D3?

Mastering a clutch pedal and manual gearshift is one of the trickiest challenges facing learner drivers, and choosing a car with an automatic transmission removes all of it. But while driving an auto is simpler than learning stick shift — D for drive, R for reverse, right pedal for go, left for stop — it may still leave you confused. You might have seen a D3 position on your car's gear shifter and had no idea what it's for or when to use it.

If you have seen a D3 mode, it's probably been on the shift panel of an older Honda or Acura with a traditional automatic transmission , one that uses planetary gears to create different ratios. Since the 1980s, most automatics have had at least four gears. Although the transmission will happily swap between them all by itself, that D3 position gives you more control.

The D in D3 stands for drive, as you've probably guessed, but selecting D3 doesn't lock the transmission into third gear. Instead, it means the transmission can use any gear up to and including third gear, but won't go any higher. On some cars with five or more gears, you might also see a D4 marking, which locks the transmission into the lowest four gears.

Automatics are big on convenience compared with the manual alternative, but they're not great on control. This is where D3 comes in. When driving downhill in a manual, rather than coasting in neutral, you're taught to put the car into a lower gear to make use of the engine braking effect. This phenomenon occurs because you're not touching the accelerator, meaning the engine's throttle is closed, which makes it harder for the pistons to move down their intake stroke.

Engine braking is useful because it takes the pressure off the conventional friction brakes bolted behind your wheels, helping to safeguard them from overheating. Automatics don't offer as much engine braking when left in their normal D mode, because they'll often stay in a high gear. By selecting D3, you force the engine to stay in a lower gear, just like shifting to third in a manual car.

That engine braking effect is also one of the reasons you might select D3 on a fun, twisty road like the Tail of the Dragon . Another is that forcing the car to stay in a lower gear makes it feel punchier when you nail the gas coming out of each curve. But don't get too excited. D3 is not the same as the sport mode on some automatic transmissions, which has a dedicated shift map that will downshift earlier and hang onto gears longer before shifting up.

Going downhill or blasting along a country road aren't the only situations when you might want to prevent your automatic transmission from changing up past third gear. It can also be handy when climbing hills or towing.

title: Darlington's First SMR Is Late and Over Budget. Ontario Needs to Rethink the Next Three
raw_summary: Ontario Power Generation has acknowledged that its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target. There is no replacement cost or completion date yet. OPG expects its engineering, cost and schedule review to be substantially complete by mid-2027. The reason matters. In its November 10 financial results , OPG identified continuing first-of-a-kind reactor engineering and its effects on construction execution and supply-chain performance. Ontario started physical work while parts of the design governing that work were still evolving. The project is now living with the consequence.
summary: Ontario Power Generation has acknowledged that its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target. There is no replacement cost or completion date yet. OPG expects its engineering, cost and schedule review to be substantially complete by mid-2027.
article_paragraphs: Ontario Power Generation has acknowledged that its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target. There is no replacement cost or completion date yet. OPG expects its engineering, cost and schedule review to be substantially complete by mid-2027.

The reason matters. In its November 10 financial results , OPG identified continuing first-of-a-kind reactor engineering and its effects on construction execution and supply-chain performance. Ontario started physical work while parts of the design governing that work were still evolving. The project is now living with the consequence.

This is not a story about a construction crew failing to install a basemat. The 2.1-million-pound reactor foundation is in place, work on the turbine building has progressed, and the cooling-water tunnel equipment has been assembled. These are real achievements. They do not settle the engineering dependencies, supplier requirements and delivery sequence for a first-of-a-kind reactor. Construction progress and schedule certainty are different things.

Megaproject researcher Bent Flyvbjerg calls the better approach “think slow, act fast.” Engineering, interfaces and execution plans need enough maturity that construction can advance without a succession of disruptive changes. Design and construction can overlap on controlled, ready-to-build work packages. Darlington’s own disclosure shows that the required boundary has not been maintained.
My TFIE Strategy Briefing on Darlington’s SMR examines the November disclosure, the historical nuclear construction record and the consequences for Ontario’s four-reactor plan.

Ontario is an unusually favourable test for the Western SMR industry. OPG operates a large nuclear fleet and has an experienced workforce, an established site, transmission infrastructure and public financial backing. GE Vernova Hitachi has extensive boiling-water reactor experience. Yet the BWRX-300 is still a new design, and the promised economies of repeat construction depend on its becoming stable enough to repeat.

The four-reactor programme originally carried a C$20.9 billion budget. Within that were C$6.1 billion for the first reactor, C$1.6 billion of common infrastructure and C$13.2 billion for Units 2 through 4. The financial proposition depends on the later reactors becoming cheaper after the first teaches suppliers and builders how to execute the design.

In my October 2025 assessment I applied historical nuclear construction reference-class uplifts rather than relying only on the project’s internal estimates. A 67% uplift to the Unit 1 reactor component, with shared infrastructure held unchanged, produces a C$11.8 billion first-stage cost. A 202% uplift produces about C$20.0 billion, or nearly 96% of the original budget for all four reactors. These are illustrative stress outcomes from the historical construction class, not new OPG estimates. They show how much of the programme’s financial margin depends on getting the first design and subsequent learning right.

article_paragraphs: Renault and Nissan India have reported encouraging month-on-month (MoM) sales growth in October 2026, with the Triber and Magnite emerging as key contributors to their respective brands’ volumes. While both automakers registered healthy sequential growth, their year-on-year (YoY) performances remained mixed. Both Renault and Nissan manufacture at the Chennai plant, which is owned by Renault.

Renault India reported total sales of 4,577 units in October 2026, registering a marginal 2% YoY decline compared to 4,672 units sold in October 2025. However, the automaker delivered a strong 35% MoM recovery over the 3,399 units dispatched in September 2026.

Renault Triber remained the brand’s highest-selling model, contributing 2,588 units to overall sales. Although volumes declined by 18% YoY, the MPV registered an impressive 48% MoM growth over September’s 1,750 units. Triber singlehandedly accounted for approximately 56.5% of Renault’s total October sales. Sales are expected to grow with the recently launch of Triber turbo and that of upcoming Triber CNG Turbo .

Renault Kwid also delivered positive performance, emerging as the second-largest contributor to the brand’s sales. This entry-level hatchback recorded 808 units, marking a robust 46% YoY growth over 554 units in October 2025. MoM volumes also increased by 40% from 577 units in September 2026.

Up next was the Duster which has recorded sales of 601 units, up 29% MoM compared to 465 units in September 2026. Duster sales are expected to pick up in coming weeks, with the recent launch of Hybrid Duster , which delivers best in class performance as well as mileage.

Meanwhile, Renault Kiger continued to face pressure. Sales stood at 580 units, suffering a steep decline of 39% YoY from 948 units and 6% MoM from 614 units in September 2026. Overall, Renault’s October performance was largely driven by the Triber and Kwid, which together accounted for nearly 74% of the company’s monthly sales.

Nissan India reported total sales of 3,594 units in October 2026, registering a healthy 37% YoY growth over 2,615 units sold in October 2025. The company also recorded a 9% MoM improvement compared to 3,300 units dispatched in September 2026.

Nissan Magnite continued to lead brand’s sales chart with 1,656 units. However, the compact SUV witnessed a 37% YoY decline compared to 2,615 units in October 2025. On a sequential basis, volumes improved by 10% over September 1,502 units.

raw_title: Which Highway Really Has The Highest Number Of Lanes?
title: Which Highway Really Has The Highest Number Of Lanes?
raw_summary: Freeways are to people what arteries are to red blood cells. Most freeways consist of three or four lanes of synchronized traffic flow (or collective halt), but have you ever wondered what the world record is for the highest number of lanes on a freeway? The obvious choice would be the Katy Freeway on I-10 just west of Houston, which has no fewer than 26 traffic lanes spread across both directions at its widest. However, that number also includes feeder roads that don't actually form part of the I-10, so it's often argued that the "true" number is actually 18. If that's the case, a few other massive highways may indeed lay claim to Katy's title as the highest-lane highway in the world. Canada, for instance, has an 18-lane road approaching one of its airports, while Burma's capital city has a section with up to 20 lanes. However, perhaps the biggest threats sit halfway across the globe in China. These include a special section of the G4 Beijing–Hong Kong-Macau Expressway and the Hefei–Nanjing Expressway, the latter of which can open up to as many as 36 separate lanes — but with one very important caveat. Let's take a look at some of the highest-lane freeways in the world and how they compare before crowning the winner.
summary: Freeways are to people what arteries are to red blood cells. Most freeways consist of three or four lanes of synchronized traffic flow (or collective halt), but have you ever wondered what the world record is for the highest number of lanes on a freeway?
article_paragraphs: Freeways are to people what arteries are to red blood cells. Most freeways consist of three or four lanes of synchronized traffic flow (or collective halt), but have you ever wondered what the world record is for the highest number of lanes on a freeway? The obvious choice would be the Katy Freeway on I-10 just west of Houston, which has no fewer than 26 traffic lanes spread across both directions at its widest. However, that number also includes feeder roads that don't actually form part of the I-10, so it's often argued that the "true" number is actually 18.

If that's the case, a few other massive highways may indeed lay claim to Katy's title as the highest-lane highway in the world. Canada, for instance, has an 18-lane road approaching one of its airports, while Burma's capital city has a section with up to 20 lanes. However, perhaps the biggest threats sit halfway across the globe in China. These include a special section of the G4 Beijing–Hong Kong-Macau Expressway and the Hefei–Nanjing Expressway, the latter of which can open up to as many as 36 separate lanes — but with one very important caveat. Let's take a look at some of the highest-lane freeways in the world and how they compare before crowning the winner.

See, this is where things get tricky. While Katy has at least 18 lanes of moving traffic at its widest, both the G4's 25-lane and the Hefei–Nanjing Expressway's 36-lane sections are actually toll crossings. For example, the G4's 25-lane Zhuozhou Toll Gate section only starts about 710 yards before the tollbooths and ends about a quarter-mile after them. Most of its 1,412-mile road network — long, but not quite enough to match the world's longest highways — is actually just four lanes in each direction. The same goes for Hefei–Nanjing Expressway, which funnels back to four lanes beyond the 36-lane Wuzhuang Toll Gate.

That's the key differentiator here. By comparison, Katy's 18 lanes consist of 12 passenger car lanes and a maximum of six for high-occupancy vehicles (HOVs), and stretches for an estimated length of 12 miles. Of course, the definition for how long a stretch of road would need to be to qualify is subjective, but what isn't subjective is the fact that one has fast-moving traffic, and the others don't. In fact, back in 2015, huge delays at the G4's Zhuozhou crossing during China's Golden Week celebrations, with drivers stacked next to each other, gave rise to false reports that the G4 had as many as 50 lanes. Still, calling a slow-moving toll plaza a highway is a stretch. But what about other highways with 18+ lanes?

If you thought Germany's Autobahn, the only highway in the world with no speed limit , staked a claim, then you'd be quite wrong. Despite its infamous reputation, the Autobahn never goes above four lanes in each direction. The 20-lane section of Yaza Htarni Road in Naypyidaw, Burma, does count, though. It was brought to widespread attention during the "Top Gear: Burma Special" episode, where James, Jeremy, and Richard were astonished at just how wide (and empty) it was. However, it only extends for about 2.5 miles (4 kilometers); it's not an actual highway, and it's mostly deserted.

Then there's the King's Highway 401 in Ontario, which matches the Katy Freeway's 18 lanes as it approaches the Pearson International Airport. This sounds particularly useful given that the highway can sometimes see up to 500,000 vehicles over the course of a day. However, at the end of the day, none of these roads really match Katy at its widest, where feeder and carpool lanes join it to form as many as 26 lanes of fast-moving traffic.

raw_title: High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine
title: High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine
raw_summary: Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks . Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

“High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”
That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors , adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the big bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

“Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines , including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

article_paragraphs: COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.

It wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.
The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.
The CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

The program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL launched its aviation unit .

CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.
~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

raw_title: What's Your Most Unforgettable Close Call?
title: What's Your Most Unforgettable Close Call?
raw_summary: People are capable of doing some supremely stupid things in cars. We've seen the warnings from informational videos over the decades , and our personal blunders and experiences have demonstrated this point, too . We can, of course, be attentive behind the wheel, but that doesn't account for the others who aren't while on the road. It's partly why dash cams and their resulting videos have gained so much traction in recent years. While someone's dumb decision may end up in disaster, others might end in close calls — moments where destruction was inches away. Close calls happen more often than you might expect, especially when we live in an era where vehicles are equipped with every warning along with literal bells and whistles to tell drivers they might hit something. This week, we don't want to know about the little near-misses — we want to know about the big ones that haunt you. Tell us about the misses that had they been hits, would've made for calamity.

Years ago, while in the city for the New York International Auto Show, I was lucky enough to be driving a well-equipped 2021 Maserati Levante GTS . I had taken it on a scenic drive along the Belt Parkway to Amityville, and on my return to Brooklyn, I hit a bit of traffic. About 10 minutes into my drive, in a 35 mph residential zone, an Audi Q5 came speeding up behind me. I reactively slowed down to let it fly past.

I watched as this Q5 blazed through a red light and hit another car, a fairly new Subaru, before the Q5 went spinning into the other side of the intersection. That was near miss number one. Two people got out of the smashed Q5 and bolted. Instinctively, I wanted to stop and help, but I was in a part of New York I was unfamiliar with in a six-figure vehicle that wasn't mine. Instead, I opted to get around the scene.

Seconds later, a Ford Taurus came up on my bumper, then quickly maneuvered ahead to cut me off before making a turn into a parking lot where it then stopped, and a cop hopped out and proceeded to stop a kid who had run from the crash scene. The Taurus was never put in park, though, and it started rolling towards the Maserati. I panicked, trying to figure out how to reverse it with its weird shifter.

The cop saw what was happening and was able to catch the car about an inch away from the Maserati. Near miss number two. Meanwhile, another cop had arrested the kid. After a deep breath and a phone call to my husband, still quite shaken, I made my way back to Brooklyn.

It might not have been the greatest near-miss, but the feelings I had nearly five years ago remain strong to this day. With that chaos in mind, what was your most unforgettable close call? Tell us all about it and why it holds critical space in your memory bank in the comments below.

article_paragraphs: A new IEA report finds renewables are already strengthening energy security and competitiveness while cutting fuel import costs—but faster electrification, grid modernization, and greater flexibility can extend these gains across the economy.

Spain’s rapid expansion of renewable power has strengthened its energy security and competitiveness, but faster electrification across transport, buildings, and industry will be essential to meeting the country’s energy and climate goals, according to a new IEA Energy Policy Review published Oct. 5, 2026.

Between 2015 and 2025, renewables’ share of Spain’s electricity generation increased from 35% to 56%, while emissions declined by around one-fifth. These achievements have been underpinned by the country’s strong energy and climate policy framework and its well-established approach to a just transition, which links clean energy investment with jobs, regional development, and social inclusion.

Spain’s growing share of renewable power is already helping to lower wholesale electricity prices and reduce its exposure to imported fuels. Without the vast expansion of renewable capacity, its natural gas imports for power generation would have been nearly 40%, or USD 26 billion, higher in 2024. Nonetheless, imports still provided almost 70% of Spain’s total energy consumption in 2024, underscoring the need to extend the transition beyond electricity supply.

Accelerating electrification of end-uses should also be a priority, the report finds. Today, electricity accounts for just 25% of Spain’s final energy consumption, well below the country’s target of 35% by 2030. Electric vehicle uptake is relatively limited, notably for corporate fleets, while fossil-fuel heating remains widespread, and the industry faces high upfront investment costs.

A combination of taxes, levies, and network charges are keeping end-user electricity prices high, while fossil fuels face comparatively lower charges in Spain. The country is taking steps to address this, including by abolishing the tax on electricity production in 2026. Further rebalancing domestic energy price dynamics, while protecting vulnerable consumers, could strengthen incentives for households and businesses to electrify and help industry capture the competitive advantages of renewable power.

Spain has launched reforms to accelerate storage, demand-side flexibility, and adapting grid rules to a rapidly changing generation mix. Continued progress on power system infrastructure and management, alongside a more balanced mix of wind, solar, and hybrid technologies, can help Spain integrate growing shares of renewable generation while strengthening electricity security and resilience.

The review also highlights the importance of carefully managing the planned nuclear phase-out to maintain security of supply. Following the recent approval to extend the lifetime operation of the Almaraz nuclear power plant, the report recommends implementing a transparent framework for future case-by-case decisions that considers the costs and benefits for consumers and the wider power system.

Daihatsu teased a new Copen with its K-Open concept last year (pictured below), and it wouldn't be hard for Toyota to throw a bit of design work at its subsidiary's kei car and bring a proper S-FR to market.

Of course, a modern kei car would be a pretty substantial rework of the S-FR formula. Previous Copens have all been front-wheel drive, so shifting to a rear-wheel-drive platform to accommodate an S-FR twin would make it more of a sports car, too. The original concept was neither modern nor kei, with a 1.5-liter naturally-aspirated four-cylinder engine and a rear seat, the former of which would be impossible and the latter unlikely in a kei car. In fact, the whole design would need to shrink to meet kei car requirements, making it even less likely we'd get a version here in the States. Still, Toyota is already bringing us one kei , so maybe we can dream.

Even if it's only for the Japanese market, I hope this report from Response is accurate and that Toyota is really thinking about bringing the S-FR to market as a Copen variant. It just makes sense — take your beloved-but-abandoned little sports car concept and apply it to your soon-to-be-resurrected little sports car platform. Maybe, if we're really lucky, Toyota will bring some over to the States as the same sort of low-speed vehicle as the KEI-01. I'd happily tune a limiter out of one of these just to get to drive it.

title: Sanrivatti One Is a V-10 Hypercar with a Motorcycle-Like Seating Position
raw_summary: It’s an age-old question: which offers the superior experience, driving a really fast car or riding a motorcycle? Well, like the kid from the old El Paso soft taco vs hard taco meme, hypercar startup Sanrivatti asks, “Why Not Both?” First shown as a concept with minimal details, there’s now a prototype out that reveals how Sanrivatti plans to marry the riding position of a motorcycle with an in-car layout. article_paragraphs: It’s an age-old question: which offers the superior experience, driving a really fast car or riding a motorcycle? Well, like the kid from the old El Paso soft taco vs hard taco meme, hypercar startup Sanrivatti asks, “Why Not Both?” First shown as a concept with minimal details, there’s now a prototype out that reveals how Sanrivatti plans to marry the riding position of a motorcycle with an in-car layout.

The car is simply called the One, and it looks quite different than other hypercars, thanks to the head-forward packaging. Carbon-fiber bodywork incorporates huge air channels around the waist, like a Ford GT, but the wraparound glass of the cockpit has the look of a spacecraft rather than earth-bound transportation.

Actually, overall, the One looks like something that could have appeared as a playable vehicle from the pre- Mario Kart Super Nintendo racing game F-Zero . Yes, this single-seat hypercar has wheels, but it’s otherwise a radical departure from what a track special would ordinarily look like.

And yes, it’ll be track only. Given the “Apex Position” blend between riding and driving, there’ll need to be a complex restraint system for the driver—or rider? Maybe we should just go with pilot. Projected specifications are pretty spicy, with a combustion engine producing 800 horsepower and a claimed curb weight of just 2425 pounds. Top speed is estimated at above 200 mph.

That power will come from racing specialist Judd, a U.K.-based racing specialist with experience in F1, IndyCar, and Le Mans. The engine will be a naturally aspirated 5.5-liter V-10, and it’ll put that power to the ground through a racing-spec Hewland six-speed sequential gearbox. Brakes are from AP Racing, wheels are forged magnesium from Braid, with racing-grade Michelin Pilot Sport tires.

A blend of Suzuki GSX-R and Audi R8 certainly sounds pretty invigorating, but driving the Sanrivatti One is going to require a complete rewiring of your brain. The car will be controlled with foot pedals for braking and acceleration, and it will have a steering wheel. However, you’ll be pressing rearward for the latter controls, and also able to lean your body into the corners while still clutching the wheel.

It’s probably going to feel like flying, both the good parts and the terrifying bits. Sanrivatti is literally leaning into this unique experience, suggesting that learning how to drive the One will kind of be the thing that sets it apart from every other hypercar out there.

If nothing else, it’s an interesting way to sidestep the usual metrics of zero-to-60-mph and Nürburgring lap times, and other numbers defined by the stopwatch. How will the Sanrivatti One compare with other hypercars? If they get it right, it simply won’t.

raw_title: 12 Plug-In Hybrids With The Longest Electric-Only Range
title: 12 Plug-In Hybrids With The Longest Electric-Only Range
raw_summary: Back in 2010, Chevrolet introduced the groundbreaking Volt — America's first plug-in hybrid production car. Packing a fairly big 16-kWh battery pack, the Volt had an EPA-estimated electric range of 35 miles, with later first-generation models rated at up to 38 miles. When the battery was depleted, it turned to a 1.4-liter four-cylinder engine with 84 horsepower to cover longer distances. Although it ultimately failed to attract enough buyers and was discontinued in 2019, the Chevrolet Volt was so far ahead of its time that many current PHEVs struggle to match its electric range. In fact, out of the 12 plug-in hybrids with the longest electric-only range on sale right now, four have lower range figures. Of course, many modern PHEVs offer more EV range, with some models, like the 2027 Land Rover Range Rover Plug-in Hybrid, 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC 350e 4MATIC, and 2027 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid, capable of delivering 50 miles of driving without calling on the internal combustion engine.

To compile this list, we evaluated the 2027 plug-in hybrids for the U.S. market, ranking them from the shortest to longest electric range based on EPA estimates. For models awaiting official 2027 figures, we used their 2026 EPA ratings, noting any powertrain changes. Excluded are models that are all-new for 2027 and not yet EPA-rated. Also, all listed prices include the destination charge. Let's dig in!

The 2027 Kia Sportage is offered with three powertrains — a 2.5-liter gas engine with 187 hp, 1.6-liter turbo-four hybrid with 232 hp, and a plug-in variant with an electric motor for 268 hp combined. However, the PHEV's added potency doesn't translate into real-world performance, as it needs the same 6.9 seconds to reach 60 mph as the regular hybrid (per Car and Driver 's testing procedure).

But this should surprise nobody, as the Sportage Plug-in Hybrid has a significantly larger and heavier 13.8-kWh battery, with the regular hybrid packing a small 1.5-kWh pack. As a result, it provides a meaningful EV-only range of 34 miles. The battery also supports Level 2 charging, so it can be fully recharged in only two hours. Once the battery is depleted, the Sportage Plug-in Hybrid doesn't turn into a gas guzzler and returns a respectable 36 mpg combined. Not bad, considering it also comes standard with AWD, unlike the gas and hybrid models, where AWD is optional.

Saving money on fuel by making the most of the PHEV's battery does require a few compromises, though. The Sportage Plug-in Hybrid starts at $42,085 in the X-Line trim, compared to $37,285 for the regular hybrid in the same trim. The hybrid Sportage is also available in lower-end trims, with the base LX costing $32,085.

The PHEV's larger battery also eats into cargo space. While the Sportage Hybrid has a big 39.5-cubic-foot trunk — only 0.1 cubic feet smaller than the gas model — the PHEV offers only 34.5 cubic feet of cargo capacity. Fortunately, there is no difference in passenger accommodation, with all Sportage models offering ample space for adults in both rows.

BMW facelifted the 7 Series for 2027 , replacing the outgoing model's convoluted fascia with a cleaner front end that actually complements its monolithic, slab-sided proportions. As is customary nowadays, the cabin got a tech upgrade, with the 7 Series now packing BMW's Panoramic iDrive system with a parallelogram-like center screen, a thin panoramic display at the base of the windshield, and even a passenger screen. Meanwhile, passengers in the rear can now use the massive 31.3-inch theater-screen for Zoom video calls thanks to the built-in camera.

title: Retaining Lawson isn't enough
raw_summary: Liam Lawson never failed at Red Bull Racing in 2025. It was Red Bull that failed Liam Lawson. Retaining his services for another year isn't just a logical decision, but perhaps the first sign that the organisation is changing the habits it developed under Helmut Marko. Yet there's perhaps one more step it needs to take to avoid failing Lawson again.–

article_paragraphs: Liam Lawson never failed at Red Bull Racing in 2025. It was Red Bull that failed Liam Lawson.

Retaining his services for another year isn't just a logical decision, but perhaps the first sign that the organisation is changing the habits it developed under Helmut Marko. Yet there's perhaps one more step it needs to take to avoid failing Lawson again.–
It needs to stop treating its young drivers – Lawson included – like goods with an expiry date.

There's hardly anyone who would disagree that the New Zealander not only deserved to stay in F1 after his performances this year, but also earned that right under the pressure of having no clarity over his future for so long. Many would probably have cracked or become frustrated, but Red Bull trained him well in how to shield himself from that pressure and not let it affect his performance.

His strongest spell of the year perhaps coincided with a period when the paddock was increasingly asking the same question, and doing so more and more loudly: what else does this guy have to do to secure his future?

The final confirmation came after a run of five races in the points, four of which he finished seventh, putting him in a class of his own in the midfield. That run also included some stunning qualifying performances and bold moves on track. He's ninth in the standings, with more than double the points of Pierre Gasly , who occupies the next position in the championship table. And it's largely thanks to Lawson's contribution that Racing Bulls now looks set to secure its best result in the team's history.

Lawson's 2026 is surely his strongest season to date, at least in F1. But it's also the first in which he's actually been able to prove what he's capable of without being called up as a stand-in or rushed into an impossible task, as happened in early 2025.

Lawson's dreadful couple of races for Red Bull perhaps didn't come as a surprise to anyone – apart, seemingly, from the organisation itself. Yet expecting him to deliver something substantially better in the circumstances of his promotion – being placed in the same garage as Max Verstappen after just 11 F1 starts – was like expecting a newly graduated medical student to perform open-heart surgery on his second day in the job. Or a firefighter being sent into a burning skyscraper on his first call, without even having rescued a cat from a tree.

title: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
raw_summary: Mention a Chevy Impala, and thoughts of an unremarkable family sedan may come to mind, but add an SS next to the nameplate and things change. The Impala SS (Super Sport) is a pure horsepower play that dates back to 1961, two years after the Bowtie brand launched the Impala as a standalone model. Its numbers are still impressive, even by 21st-century standards. The retail version of the Impala SS from the 1960s, which covered two generations, produced up to 425 horsepower. The later Impala SS generations from the 1990s and 2000s were less brutish, offering between 240 and 303 hp, but they were still a step up from their more mundane counterparts. However, these horsepower numbers come with a catch. The output figures for 1960s Impala SS models reflected gross horsepower ratings, which generally didn't account for intake, exhaust, and accessory loads. When the 1970s rolled around, the auto industry was dealing with tighter emissions regulations and insurance companies that took a dim view of high-powered cars. By the 1972 model year, Detroit switched to net horsepower calculations to better reflect real-world engine configurations. Because gross horsepower ratings often varied from manufacturer to manufacturer, there's no standard way to convert horsepower ratings between the methods, but both still measure horsepower at the crankshaft, not the wheels.

article_paragraphs: Mention a Chevy Impala, and thoughts of an unremarkable family sedan may come to mind, but add an SS next to the nameplate and things change. The Impala SS (Super Sport) is a pure horsepower play that dates back to 1961, two years after the Bowtie brand launched the Impala as a standalone model. Its numbers are still impressive, even by 21st-century standards. The retail version of the Impala SS from the 1960s, which covered two generations, produced up to 425 horsepower. The later Impala SS generations from the 1990s and 2000s were less brutish, offering between 240 and 303 hp, but they were still a step up from their more mundane counterparts.

However, these horsepower numbers come with a catch. The output figures for 1960s Impala SS models reflected gross horsepower ratings, which generally didn't account for intake, exhaust, and accessory loads. When the 1970s rolled around, the auto industry was dealing with tighter emissions regulations and insurance companies that took a dim view of high-powered cars. By the 1972 model year, Detroit switched to net horsepower calculations to better reflect real-world engine configurations. Because gross horsepower ratings often varied from manufacturer to manufacturer, there's no standard way to convert horsepower ratings between the methods, but both still measure horsepower at the crankshaft, not the wheels.

Our ranking of every Impala SS generation by power takes into account the highest advertised horsepower ratings for regular-production SS models, regardless of whether it's gross or net. Special race versions and modified cars are excluded. Here's how every Impala SS generation compares in maximum power output.

The first Impala was a variant of the 1958 Bel Air, but the SS designation didn't arrive until the third-generation Impala in 1961. The second generation, without a Super Sport option, filled the two-year gap as the free-standing Impala model. The first Impala SS model's power output is a story of progression. The 1961 Impala SS arrived with a choice of V8 engines: 348-cubic-inch units rated at 305, 340, or 350 horsepower and a 409-cubic-inch V8 officially rated at 360 horsepower. In 1962, that king-of-the-hill powerplant could also be configured with dual four-barrel carburetors, increasing output to 409 horsepower.

Thanks to solid lifters, dual exhausts, and an 11:1 compression ratio, the 409's output rose to 425 gross horsepower for the 1963 model year. Chevy history buffs may also recall a 1963 Z11 lightweight drag-racing Impala with a 430-horsepower 427-cubic-inch V8. Keep in mind that this one wasn't a Super Sport model, nor was it a part of regular production, as only 57 were ever produced. The 1964 Impala SS continued with the same 409 from the previous year.

Horsepower for the second iteration of the Impala SS was in familiar territory, with peak outputs sitting at 425, but the Impala eventually took a different route to get there. To start, Chevy launched an entirely new Impala with a sleeker exterior and a perimeter frame, ditching the X-type architecture of the outgoing model. The new looks helped the 1965 Impala become the best-selling single model of all time. A record 1,046,514 units were sold, with roughly 23% being SS variants. Impala SS examples from this generation still attract a lot of attention online .

The top engine for the non-SS 1965 Impala was the familiar Turbo-Fire 409-cubic-inch V8, making 400 horsepower. For the SS, Chevy also offered the L78 V8, a 396-cubic-inch V8 rated at 425 gross horsepower. A year later, the L72 427-cubic-inch V8 joined the options list, also rated for up to 425 hp. The powerplant featured a forged crankshaft and pistons, solid lifters, and a dual exhaust system. The SS 427 continued into 1967 and 1968, but with a slightly different L36 engine, still with 427 cubic inches, but now rated at 385 hp. In 1969, output increased to 390 hp.

The final Impala SS came with 303 hp, which is the most of any modern generation. The supercharged V6 in the previous eighth-generation SS was replaced with a naturally aspirated 5.3-liter LS4 V8. That results in a zero-to-60 mph dash of 5.6 seconds, which is on par with a modern-day Mazda Miata – but remember, this was 20 years ago.

raw_title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
raw_summary: Technically, directional tires can be rotated from one side of a car to the other. Nobody can stop you from unbolting a wheel/tire combo from one side of the car and putting it on the other side. The catch is that doing it properly involves more work than unbolting the wheels and swapping their positions. Skip that extra work and those carefully designed tread patterns will end up running backward. That might not sound all that terrible, but for these "unidirectional" tires, the rolling direction matters. Crossing directional tires requires removing them from their wheels and remounting them in the correct orientation for the opposite side. Each one then needs rebalancing, which is where the red and yellow dots on tires come in. So sure, you can unbolt whatever is on the passenger side of your car and swap it to the driver's side. But the tread will be heading in the wrong direction. Still, there are other ways to do this job without messing anything up.
summary: Technically, directional tires can be rotated from one side of a car to the other. Nobody can stop you from unbolting a wheel/tire combo from one side of the car and putting it on the other side. The catch is that doing it properly involves more work than unbolting the wheels and swapping their positions.
article_paragraphs: Technically, directional tires can be rotated from one side of a car to the other. Nobody can stop you from unbolting a wheel/tire combo from one side of the car and putting it on the other side. The catch is that doing it properly involves more work than unbolting the wheels and swapping their positions. Skip that extra work and those carefully designed tread patterns will end up running backward. That might not sound all that terrible, but for these "unidirectional" tires, the rolling direction matters.

Crossing directional tires requires removing them from their wheels and remounting them in the correct orientation for the opposite side. Each one then needs rebalancing, which is where the red and yellow dots on tires come in. So sure, you can unbolt whatever is on the passenger side of your car and swap it to the driver's side. But the tread will be heading in the wrong direction. Still, there are other ways to do this job without messing anything up.

Some owners will simply swap the rear tires onto the front and vice versa, keeping each tire on the same side of the car. Of course, that only helps if you have what we call a "square" fitment. That means that all four of your wheels and tires are the same size. Other owners have larger rear wheels and tires, so such a swap wouldn't work. Most major tire brands offer unidirectional tires, and the restrictions come down to how the tread itself meets the road.

Directional tires are designed to roll in a specific direction during forward travel. Their tread often features a recognizable V-shaped pattern, with channels arranged to move water away from the contact patch to help prevent hydroplaning . A wheel with the directional tire pointed the wrong way won't grip as effectively, which can cut into braking performance on wet roads.

Thankfully, there's a very simple way to check. Directional tires typically have an arrow marking on the sidewall indicating how the tire should roll. Once installed on the wheel and vehicle, the arrow should face forward when it's at the top of the wheel. The directional nature of a tire can benefit drivers on multiple surfaces. Snow, rain, and mud can all clear the contact patch more easily, in some cases, if the rotation direction is correct. In fact, a tire's tread pattern can affect winter performance more than its width .

Let's imagine that you have a square setup and directional tires. The easiest way to rotate said tires is simply to swap them between axles on the same side. So your front tires would move to the rear, and your rears would move up front. The trade-off is that the tires may wear less evenly and more quickly. Some folks go further and swap them both from front to back and from one side to the other, but that means having the tires dismounted from the wheels, remounted, and balanced again. Still others will simply swap tires from one side to the other and forgo moving them from one axle to the other, which requires the same extra work.

For a staggered setup, things are trickier. Because the tires can't go from front to back, rotating them requires dismounting all four tires from the wheels and then remounting them on the opposite side of the same axle. The job can be time-consuming and costly, but it can help even out wear between the left and right tires. As is the case for most tire-changing needs, a qualified shop is probably the best bet. Not only does it save you the work of doing it, but a shop is going to be familiar with everything we've discussed here.

raw_title: Mini Truck Vs. Side-By-Side: What Are The Practical Differences?
title: Mini Truck Vs. Side-By-Side: What Are The Practical Differences?
raw_summary: You've likely seen those neat little mini trucks from Japan. They're the size of a compact vehicle, but have a bed as long as some full-size pickups. These Kei trucks, as they are called, look like they would be pretty practical for a number of uses. President Trump was quite smitten with Kei trucks when he saw them in Japan, apparently for the first time, later calling them "really cute." And in a December 2025 Truth Social post, he said that he had "approved" the manufacture of these "tiny" vehicles here. But, as is the case with many of the president's statements, no one is quite sure what that means. Unfortunately, you can't buy a new one for road use in the U.S., but older ones are available thanks to an exception in import laws.

article_paragraphs: You've likely seen those neat little mini trucks from Japan. They're the size of a compact vehicle, but have a bed as long as some full-size pickups. These Kei trucks, as they are called, look like they would be pretty practical for a number of uses.

President Trump was quite smitten with Kei trucks when he saw them in Japan, apparently for the first time, later calling them "really cute." And in a December 2025 Truth Social post, he said that he had "approved" the manufacture of these "tiny" vehicles here. But, as is the case with many of the president's statements, no one is quite sure what that means. Unfortunately, you can't buy a new one for road use in the U.S., but older ones are available thanks to an exception in import laws.

Maybe you're thinking about snagging one of these trucks for your farm, ranch, or construction site and wondering how they compare to those side-by-sides that are made for work. These utility task vehicles (UTVs) also have a bed on the back and are often used to haul small loads around on a worksite. There are several differences. For one thing, you can easily find new UTVs for sale. Their payload and towing capacities are often higher than those of most Kei trucks. They are built more for off-roading, while Kei trucks are built for the street. It really comes down to what your needs are, though.

Kei trucks were not made to meet U.S. safety and environmental standards. The Clean Air Act prohibits importing a vehicle that doesn't meet federal emissions standards unless it's at least 21 years old. Federal law also bans foreign vehicles less than 25 years old that don't meet safety standards.

Newer Kei trucks can be imported only as off-road vehicles, permanently limited to 25 mph. That means if you want one for the road, you're stuck shopping for used Kei trucks that are at least 25 years old. That's not to say they're hard to find. Type "used Kei truck for sale" into Google and you'll see several listings for Kei trucks, as well as businesses that sell them. And the ones we've seen look to be in better shape than the typical 25- or 30-year-old vehicle, on the outside at least.

It's a bit more straightforward with UTVs, or side-by-sides. They are off-road vehicles, so they are perfectly legal to sell brand-new in the U.S. We found 25 Polaris dealerships and at least 30 Honda Powersports dealerships in the state of Florida alone. Of course, there are plenty of used side-by-sides all over the place, as well. Sites like ATV Trader, ATVHunt, and Autotrader all contain several listings.

You're going to get a longer, more versatile bed with a mini truck than you will with a UTV. Anyone can see that just by looking at the two vehicles. Kei truck beds are often over 6 feet long and over 4 feet wide. With the tailgate down, that's big enough to haul a piece of plywood or drywall, with just a little bit hanging over the edge.

The sides of a Kei truck's bed often fold down, allowing for easy loading of a packed pallet by a forklift. The walls are not very high, which makes it easier to load and offload the bed, as well. Beds on UTVs are often much smaller, with the boxes on some models being around 3.5 feet in length and a little over 4 feet in width.

raw_title: The Test Bed For Jaguar's XJ220 Twin-Turbo V6 Was A Ford Transit Van
title: The Test Bed For Jaguar's XJ220 Twin-Turbo V6 Was A Ford Transit Van
raw_summary: Jaguar is in a strange place right now because it's wedged between two very different versions of itself. In front lies a future defined by a bold design language and electric powertrains, ushered in by perhaps the most divisive car in a generation: the 1,015-hp, 400-mile 2028 Type 01 sedan . Behind it is a century-old story about craftsmanship, passion, and a great big dollop of supercharger whine. There was the absolutely stunning E-Type, which Enzo Ferrari famously christened as the most beautiful car in the world, and let's not forget the bonkers V12-powered XJR-9 that not only won Le Mans, but was voted as one of your favorite sports prototype race cars of all time . Then there's the XJ220 — arguably the most curious chapter of them all. It had a difficult start to life because Jaguar opted for a last-minute switch from a V12 to a twin-turbo V6 and from all-wheel drive to rear-wheel drive, instantly making it less sexy and appealing to customers than rivals like the Bugatti EB110 and Ferrari F40. Instead, the XJ220 did its talking with sheer force, clocking a 217-mph top speed to become the world's fastest production car in 1992. Imagine how smug its engineers felt.

article_paragraphs: Jaguar is in a strange place right now because it's wedged between two very different versions of itself. In front lies a future defined by a bold design language and electric powertrains, ushered in by perhaps the most divisive car in a generation: the 1,015-hp, 400-mile 2028 Type 01 sedan . Behind it is a century-old story about craftsmanship, passion, and a great big dollop of supercharger whine. Then there's the XJ220 — arguably the most curious chapter of them all. It had a difficult start to life because Jaguar opted for a last-minute switch from a V12 to a twin-turbo V6 and from all-wheel drive to rear-wheel drive, instantly making it less sexy and appealing to customers than rivals like the Bugatti EB110 and Ferrari F40. Instead, the XJ220 did its talking with sheer force, clocking a 217-mph top speed to become the world's fastest production car in 1992. Imagine how smug its engineers felt.

What's interesting about its twin-turbo V6 is how it was tested. We all know manufacturers use test mule cars to iron out any pre-production issues, but these normally have some sort of resemblance to the final car. For the XJ220, Jaguar and its development partner Tom Walkinshaw Racing (TWR) decided to use a humble Ford Transit. Yes, a Ford Transit. If you're thinking this sounds familiar, it's because it was the same vehicle Richard Hammond used in a drag race against a Holden Maloo truck, when the original "Top Gear" trio competed against their Aussie counterparts.

Most likely, discretion. The XJ220 was a tight-lipped secret around the Jaguar offices, and when TWR had finalized the engine setup and wanted to run its various litmus tests, it had to do so very carefully. So, what better to use to disguise your shiny new, world-record-chasing motor than something absolutely nobody would suspect?

Based on a 1989 long-wheelbase Ford Transit, the exterior looked almost identical to a slightly worn example, with the only potential giveaway being the ZR performance tires and identical alloy wheels to those that would eventually end up on the XJ220. But if you were to open up the cargo bed, you'd spot the 3.5-liter twin-turbo V6 — originally rated at 540 horsepower — and suspiciously racy running gear lurking low down.

An interesting fact is that this engine is actually closely related to the engine in the MG 6R4 — a monstrous rally car, and arguably the only cool car MG has ever built . You see, the 6R4 was built for Group B, which ended in 1986, and thus meant MG had no use for a properly decked-out six-cylinder engine anymore. It then reportedly sold the rights and design infrastructure to TWR, and that's how it eventually wound up in the XJ220.

If you thought it was heading for a peaceful retirement in the Scottish Highlands, you'd be dead wrong. Once TWR had finished work with it, the Transit was acquired by the Benetton Formula 1 team, which used it as a parts delivery vehicle. It might have been on the verge of being scrapped after Benetton was done with it, but then, in stepped a savior: Don Law Racing.

Don Law Racing is widely considered to be the world's leading XJ220 specialist. The rightful heir to the Frankenstein Transit project, then. The company worked on the vehicle and got it back up to condition, and once it eventually did, it appeared in places like the Goodwood Festival of Speed, where it has indeed been up the hill on multiple occasions and left unsuspecting spectators in awe. Quite the fairy-tale ending, wouldn't you say?

title: 2027 Tata Nexon Spied With Big Changes Inside & Out
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The next-generation Nexon is expected to bring a more upright design, a thoroughly updated cabin and a new platform The Tata Nexon is gearing up for its first full-generation change since its arrival in 2017. Fresh spy shots of the upcoming model have now offered a closer look at the exterior and interior, suggesting that Tata Motors is preparing a more substantial update than the usual mid-life refresh. The test vehicle remains heavily camouflaged, so the final design is still under wraps. However, there are a few noticeable changes. The new Nexon appears to have a boxier profile, with a more upright front section and a flatter roofline. The revised proportions could also help free up more headroom for rear passengers and improve luggage space, although Tata has not revealed any dimensions or boot capacity figures. The familiar Nexon silhouette hasn’t been completely abandoned, but the next-generation model appears to have a more traditional SUV stance. The circular wheel arches, rectangular ORVMs with integrated indicators and conventional pull-type door handles seem to have been retained. Pic Source: supercarsandbikesjammu The spy shots also reveal a new alloy wheel design. The test mule appears to be running 17-inch wheels, while higher variants could get larger 18-inch units. The rear is expected to receive redesigned tail lamps and a reworked bumper, with changes to the front grille, headlamps and bumper likely as well. The interior appears to be getting a more noticeable makeover. The latest images show a slimmer digital instrument cluster and a larger touchscreen infotainment system. The two displays could get a revised interface and additional connected features. Pic Source: carstatsglo The familiar two-spoke steering wheel with the illuminated Tata logo appears to have been carried over, although some detailing and switchgear changes are possible. Other features being tipped for the new Nexon include a panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, ambient lighting, an air purifier and a built-in DVR. A 360-degree camera and Level 2 ADAS could also feature on the equipment list. However, Tata has yet to confirm these additions. The next-generation Nexon is expected to move to Tata’s modular ATLAS platform, which can accommodate ICE, CNG and electric powertrains. The existing 1.2-litre turbo-petrol engine is expected to continue, while the diesel could receive the newer Kryojet unit seen on the Sierra. The current petrol and CNG options are also expected to remain part of the range. Pic Source: supercarsandbikesjammu Tata has not announced a launch date or confirmed the new Nexon’s specifications. With testing underway, a 2027 debut is expected. The Nexon EV is also likely to receive a next-generation update, with styling cues shared with its ICE sibling.

article_paragraphs: After entering the list of the top 5 electric car brands in India, VinFast seems to be aiming to achieve similar success in the electric two-wheeler segment . Towards that end, a number of design patents have been filed this year. Building on that, VinFast has now filed patents for a new electric motorcycle and an electric scooter.

Patent images reveal a classic design approach, with smooth, curvy panels across the bodywork. A similar design was previously seen with the VinFast Vento S, which was showcased at the 2025 Bharat Mobility Expo. While using a largely retro-inspired theme, the new electric scooter patented also gets some quirky elements such as a triangular headlamp with an integrated DRL element.

While visually attractive, the smooth panelling could also be functionally relevant, helping reduce aerodynamic drag. Other key features include a broad front fender, ‘V’ badging on the front apron, and geometric-style turn indicators. The scooter has oval-shaped rear view mirrors, a flat floorboard, a wide and comfy seat and a chunky grab rail.

At the rear, the scooter gets a V-style horizontally positioned tail lamp. This new electric scooter has a different hardware setup such as a side-mounted motor. This is different from other VinFast electric scooters, all of which use a hub-mounted motor. The scooter’s premium styling and features like a side-mounted motor suggest that it could be positioned as a premium offering. One can also notice disc brakes at both ends, which is typically seen with premium scooters.

Other details such as motor output, battery pack and range have not been revealed. However, the specs could be similar to Vento S, even though that scooter is no longer available in any market. Vento S had a similar design approach and was equipped with a side-mounted motor. It had a 3.5 kWh LFP battery, offering a range of up to 160 km. Top speed of the scooter was 89 km/h. The electric motor generated 5.2 kW or approx. 7 PS of max power.

With features like large, track-ready tyres at both ends, an aggressive riding stance and a massive housing for the electric powertrain, VinFast’s new electric motorcycle is positioned as a performance-oriented machine. This is one of the several high-performance electric bikes that VinFast is working on.

So far, the names that have surfaced include the Subab, a street bike called Surad, a cruiser named Sudub and a supersport bike called Sulad. All of these will be based on VinFast’s electric platform concept. While specs of the bike have not been revealed, some reports in Vietnam claim max power output of 50 kW or 68 PS. For street-legal use, the top speed could be capped at around 130 km/h.

While targeting electric two-wheeler buyers, VinFast could also be planning to launch ebike taxi services in India. The company already offers such services in its home market Vietnam. The ebike taxi service will be something similar to the VinFast Green SM electric car taxi service , which is currently available in select cities. However, there is no official confirmation.

title: Inside Turkey's revamp for the return of a modern F1 classic
raw_summary: Finding the right balance is often a challenge in modern Formula 1. That applies to the technical regulations: striking a balance between satisfying drivers and purists on the one hand, and delivering the spectacle F1 wants to offer younger fans on the other, with a constant stream of overtaking moves for, let’s say, the TikTok generation. But that balancing act also applies to the calendar and the venues F1 visits. Many of the recently added destinations are temporary circuits in glamorous locations such as Miami, Las Vegas and Madrid, but these are not necessarily the tracks that get diehard fans excited.
summary: Finding the right balance is often a challenge in modern Formula 1. That applies to the technical regulations: striking a balance between satisfying drivers and purists on the one hand, and delivering the spectacle F1 wants to offer younger fans on the other, with a constant stream of overtaking moves for, let’s say, the TikTok generation.
article_paragraphs: Finding the right balance is often a challenge in modern Formula 1. That applies to the technical regulations: striking a balance between satisfying drivers and purists on the one hand, and delivering the spectacle F1 wants to offer younger fans on the other, with a constant stream of overtaking moves for, let’s say, the TikTok generation.

But that balancing act also applies to the calendar and the venues F1 visits. Many of the recently added destinations are temporary circuits in glamorous locations such as Miami, Las Vegas and Madrid, but these are not necessarily the tracks that get diehard fans excited.

Next year, however, a race will return to the calendar that has the potential to combine the best of both worlds. Istanbul is a global city – the bridge between Europe and Asia – and therefore the kind of destination F1 likes to have on its calendar. But the circuit, located on the Asian side of the Bosphorus, is also one that appeals to drivers and fans, particularly because of its famous Turn 8.

Ahead of the Turkish Grand Prix's return, Motorsport.com sat down with Eren Uclertopragi, president of the Turkish Automobile Federation (TOSFED). He shares the ambition of bringing both aspects together: an event that meets the standards of modern F1, while retaining a circuit that diehard fans enjoy.

“Yes, I think the same,” Uclertopragi said. “From a fans’ perspective, we are always more eager to watch the races in old-school tracks, so it's good that F1 accepted our proposal and that we are back on track. We all miss the old races, but at the end of the day, from the commercial side, we also need the races like Madrid. We need both, the modern street tracks and tracks like Istanbul, Monza and Silverstone.”

That said, all permanent circuits have to adapt to meet the standards of modern F1, both in terms of facilities and the overall presentation of the event. The layout in Istanbul will remain intact, but a great deal will change around it.

“There will be major upgrades to the circuit,” Uclertopragi explained. “We will modernize our circuit to the level F1 reaches right now. We are, of course, working on the infrastructural side. We will try to cover most of the grandstands and we will try to make fan zones to do whatever is necessary to give the best experience to the fans.”

That last point is a crucial pillar of the plans. Istanbul Park has been a drivers’ favourite in the past, but according to Uclertopragi, the biggest challenge for the next five years – the duration of the new contract – is to make it a fan favourite as well; there is a lot of work to be done in that respect.

title: Why Williams has turned Sainz and Albon into test drivers
raw_summary: Williams duo Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon have become arguably the most overqualified test drivers in the world as the team has sacrificed parts of the final Formula 1 weekends this season to help its 2027 car. As the Williams narrative has turned almost entirely to making progress for next year, Sainz and Albon have been conducting very different programmes in Friday practice to other drivers, and talking more about the value of experimental work outweighing that of absolutely nailing the preparation of a given weekend.
summary: Williams duo Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon have become arguably the most overqualified test drivers in the world as the team has sacrificed parts of the final Formula 1 weekends this season to help its 2027 car.
article_paragraphs: Williams duo Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon have become arguably the most overqualified test drivers in the world as the team has sacrificed parts of the final Formula 1 weekends this season to help its 2027 car.

As the Williams narrative has turned almost entirely to making progress for next year, Sainz and Albon have been conducting very different programmes in Friday practice to other drivers, and talking more about the value of experimental work outweighing that of absolutely nailing the preparation of a given weekend.
Asked by The Race if that made him a test driver for this part of the year, Sainz said: "I am. And I told the team that I don't care about finishing 15th or 17th.
"It's more how much can I learn, how much can they learn, in order to get myself and the team and the car in a better place for next year."

Though Williams's 2026 problems are well established it is important to understand the core issues – and the reality Williams faced in addressing them – to appreciate what it is doing right now in turning Sainz and Albon into willing, glorified test drivers.
New rules and the best engine on the grid were meant to help Williams build on Sainz's two podiums in 2025 but hopes of this being achieved in 2026 were abandoned very early.

It was the only team that failed to get a car to January's Barcelona shakedown, and the car that arrived late in Bahrain was also overweight and slow. The turnaround since has been minimal in relative performance, hence Williams is ninth of the 11 teams on points, and on single-lap pace, ahead of only Aston Martin and Cadillac in both metrics and slipping closer to both (and behind in the case of Aston Martin) as the season has worn on.

Though the weight has since come off the car, the deeper flaw was its high-rake aerodynamic concept. Aston Martin took a similar route and abandoned it with an in-season B-spec car, Williams decided doing that would cost too much.
