We literally built machines that defy the will of the gods, zoom across our skies, and let us travel in ways we were never meant to travel. Should I have been able to pull off a whirlwind visit to Boston while living in Georgia? Probably not, but the miracle of flight made it possible, and there's always going to be some thing special about sitting in a window seat that lets you see the beautiful world beneath you. Los Angeles isn't the prettiest city in the world, but even LA looks incredible from 10,000 or 15,000 feet.

With the window seat, you'll also have an easier time napping on your flight, and air travel takes so much time out of your day, you could probably use a snooze. Yes, most seats now have those bendy headrests that are supposed to make napping a little easier, but nothing beats using a sweater as a pillow and leaning against the plane. The bendy headrests can try, but while they're better than nothing, they still don't work all that great. All humans need to sleep, so book a window seat, enjoy the view, and then take a nice nap once the plane makes it above the clouds.

Does going to the bathroom get a little awkward? Sure, but there's no reason you have to drink four whiskey cokes before you board your flight. They have edibles for that now. Any time you get up to go to the bathroom, that's also the opportunity to make a new friend. Most importantly, if everyone who reads this ends up fighting over those beautiful views from the window, there will be more aisle seats available for me to take. Michelle may have a point, but I still prefer the aisle and will not be changing my mind.

title: US government grounds all flights across the United States 'due to extraordinary circumstances
raw_summary: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday afternoon that it has grounded all flights across the United States due to “extraordinary circumstances” and issues related to safety. The FAA’s website said the cause is an “equipment outage.” The site itself was down for a brief period at the time of publication, with a note that the website was “experiencing technical difficulties.”

article_paragraphs: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday afternoon that it has grounded all flights across the United States due to “extraordinary circumstances” and issues related to safety.

The FAA’s website said the cause is an “equipment outage.” The site itself was down for a brief period at the time of publication, with a note that the website was “experiencing technical difficulties.”

Per an alert sent by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center , or ATCSCC, the FAA said the ground stop means that aircraft cannot take off from departure gates. The message said that the disruption was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” but did not specify further. The alert was not visible on the ATCSCC website at press time.
The alert stated that all departing flights must remain on the ground “until further notice.” Inbound international flights will be “managed on a case-by-case basis,” it said.

A spokesperson for the FAA told TechCrunch that it issued the ground stop “following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” which manage the airspace across the United States.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X : “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

It’s not clear what caused the ongoing FAA equipment outage. The outage comes in the same week that the administration rolled out an AI-powered tool for air traffic controllers to save aircraft flight time and fuel costs — though it’s unclear if the ongoing outage is related.

Speaking to reporters outside the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that there is “no indication yet that this was a nefarious act,” but warned that the recovery “is going to take some time.”

title: FAA's Nationwide Ground Stop Definitely Not Because Of New AI Air Traffic Control Tool... Probably
raw_summary: At 3:45 p.m. ET on Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop, halting all flights that were set to take off from U.S. airports until further notice. An ATCSCC advisory was posted by Flightradar24 on Bluesky, which reads: "Due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety. Attention all aircraft operators, by order of the Federal Aviation Command Center all airports are ground stopped. All departing traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice. Inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis." The initial announcement stated the ground stop is scheduled to stay in effect until 11:00 p.m. ET, but that could change. ( Flightradar has an ongoing live blog here .) I n a Twitter post a short time later, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, "The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them." According to News9 Oklahoma, reports from aviation monitoring account OSINTdefender said the FAA's ground stop is due to communication frequency issues affecting the National Airspace System. In a short post, the FAA said , "There has been a temporary telecommunications outage – out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."

FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them." In a short post, the FAA said , "There has been a temporary telecommunications outage – out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."

In about as funny a turn of events as you could possibly imagine, our team found out about this situation from a social media post by Flavor Flav , who seems to be one of the first people to post about it. This is a developing story, and we'll update you as we learn more.

A scan of the National Airspace System Status website shows major airports listed as "airport closure," "ground stop," "ground delay," or "departure delay." The last time the FAA enacted a ground stop was in January 2023, when all domestic departures were paused for less than two hours because of a pilot notification system went down. Before that, the last ground stop had been on September 11, 2001.

A few days ago we told you about how the FAA is getting rid of ATC's floppy disks , and just yesterday it started rolling out a new AI air traffic tool . While there's nothing concrete to suggest the AI system had anything to do with the outage, Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin stood in front of some cameras to answer questions from the media, and he didn't outright deny that AI had anything to do with it making sure to say "we call it SI, remember," and that "we can't rule out anything at this point." He did say there are no indications of the outages being caused by a cyberattack or terror threat, but when asked again whether AI caused the problem, he said, "we're looking at that, that's part of something that obviously through CISA at DHS we're taking a look, we're working with our counterparts at all agencies."

He also said , "I don't want to say that this is a crisis, but it is, because we had to do a nationwide ground stoppage," and that Duffy is doing "a phenomenal job in crisis mode." When asked if it will be days or weeks before the problem is resolved, Mullin said it's too early to tell. Great!

Our very own Andy Kalmowitz is caught up in this mess, as he was about to take off from Chicago O'Hare International Airport on a connecting flight while on his way home from driving the new Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid . Right as they were getting ready to taxi the ground stop was issued, and his pilot came over the intercom and explained the situation: "We're in a nationwide ground stop right now. That's not ground delay, that's ground stop. Basically the FAA has said, 'look, we're having radio problems at multiple centers across the nation; it's not just United Airlines, and it's not just Chicago. If you're airborne, that's great, you're coming in to land,' but they are not allowing anyone else to take off and get out there into the system. Which is understandable, but I don't like it, and I know you don't either." On CNN, Pete Muntean said , "this large scale radio frequency outage has caused pilots to resort to the emergency frequency that pilots use as a last resort."

BYD announced on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.
The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).
All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

raw_title: How The Developers Of '007 First Light' Nailed The Feeling Of Being James Bond Through Its Cars And Vehicles
title: How The Developers Of '007 First Light' Nailed The Feeling Of Being James Bond Through Its Cars And Vehicles
raw_summary: As a massive fan of the James Bond franchise , my main hope going into "007 First Light" wasn't that it would have characters and plot points I recognized or have all the right bits of fan service — I just wanted the game to evoke the same emotions that the Bond movies do, to really feel like I was being Bond when playing. Luckily the game delivered those feelings in spades. IO Interactive, best known for the "Hitman" franchise, created one of the best pieces of James Bond media ever, and a big part of "First Light's" success is down to the vehicles you get to drive as Bond and how they're woven into the main story. To learn more about the game's development, and the creation of the new DLC missions that feature the Aston Martin Valhalla , I hopped on a call with Rasmus Poulsen, the game's art director, and Dominic Vega, audio director and game director of live content/missions. "We knew from the get-go that we wanted as wide a range of driving experiences as we could manage to squeeze in the game, and of course that means everything from the unexpected to the hoped for," said Poulsen, and man did they deliver.

"We knew from the get-go that we wanted as wide a range of driving experiences as we could manage to squeeze in the game, and of course that means everything from the unexpected to the hoped for," said Poulsen, and man did they deliver.

SPOILER ALERT: While I won't be talking about major plot or character spoilers in this story, I do spoil all of the various vehicular scenes and moments, so if you haven't played or finished the game yet, bookmark this page and come back to it later.

The first excellent car moment comes in one of the very first missions, when Bond is going through initial training to join the reborn 00 program. At a facility in Malta, Bond gets thrown the keys to a 2006 Aston Martin DBS, the same car seen in "Casino Royale" and "Quantum of Solace." It's described as "a classic" by one of Bond's compatriots, who adds it's "seen some real-life action too back in her day. Still a gorgeous drive." She's not lying — the DBS is totally banged up, covered in duct tape and zip ties.

Bond proceeds to race around a course, smashing through boxes and jumping down staircases. Despite how realistic the cars look and sound the handling is definitely on the arcade side of things, but it's also very fun. You're encouraged to do handbrake turns and always keep the throttle pinned, and enough actual skill and good driving is needed to do well in this mission and subsequent ones.

It's not a very long sequence, with Bond quickly moving on to other parts of training, but it's a great way to get us car people excited at the beginning of the game. This particular choice of car this early on is a great nod to our outgoing Bond on the silver screen, too. Bond movies have always had car chases, but it wasn't until the Daniel Craig films that the chases really leveled up, becoming grittier and more realistic and more exciting, sometimes the most blockbuster-y set pieces in the entire movie.

A few missions later, Bond and his fellow 00 trainees have to infiltrate a chess tournament at the Grand Carpathian Hotel in Slovakia, and they drive up in a 2007 Jaguar XJ, with Bond dressed as a chauffeur. This is where the game really nails the Bond feeling, with the regular cars and seemingly mundane scenes, and it was this aspect of putting cars in the game that Poulsen and Vega enjoyed the most. "The Bond franchise is not only about the low end and the high end, it's also about the sleeper cars. It's about getting the car people to go, 'I see you,' and it's for us to go, 'we see you too.' The middle of the pack there is really exciting to me," Poulsen said.

"Each of the Bond movies, the best ones, are a cohort of bands. Think of the curation of the cast of vehicles in the movie," Vega added. "We're making an 18-hour experience, we want to make sure that the cast of vehicles gets the nod [from fans]. It gets the 'ah OK, I see what you're doing there, oh you're doing a twist here, oh it's 'Living Daylights.'" The development team was in contact with Aston Martin and Jaguar Land Rover from the very beginning, and they knew they wanted to include a big variety of cars. "There's partnerships that you have to do with Bond, right, it's not Bond without certain vehicles in the mix, but then you still always want to surprise, you want to ' and' the expectation. The player should absolutely have their fantasy met, ' and' . I think it's really nice when people in the car world notice that," he said.

raw_summary: It’s one of just 135 Hemi Superbirds, and none has a racing history quite like it. article_paragraphs: It’s one of just 135 Hemi Superbirds, and none has a racing history quite like it.

One of the world's most famous Plymouth Hemi Superbirds is heading to auction in January, and it may leave car collectors wondering if they really need that new Italian supercar. Back in 1975, it hit 220 mph, which is faster than a Lamborghini Revuelto and a Ferrari 849 Testarossa .

While a Hemi-powered Superbird can fetch as much as $1.2 million , this particular American performance car icon is especially noteworthy. It was purchased new by the Lindsley family and used as a land speed racer between 1970 and 1988 at the El Mirage dry lake bed and Bonneville Salt Flats. In 1971, Jim and Larry Lindsley became the first father-son team to break 200 mph with this car, logging a dizzying one-way top speed of 206 mph.

Jim and Larry weren't satisfied. They continued to compete in the Superbird for several years, later swapping in race-prepped engines and, in 1975, breaking the 220-mph barrier. Evidently, the Plymouth's towering rear wing was actually functional and wasn't just there for show.

Mecum Auctions is selling the car on January 15. Years after the car retired from racing, the original 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8 was reinstalled as part of a comprehensive restoration in 2000. Five years ago, it was restored for a second time and now has the same white racing livery that it had in 1970 and 1971. It went on to serve as the official pace car for several NASCAR races at Houston Motorsports Park in 2023.

The car presents beautifully. The white paint appears to be in good condition, as are the chrome rear bumper and the black wheels, shod in Goodyear tires. It's a similar story in the cabin, where the black and white vinyl seats have aged gracefully. A look at the odometer shows the Superbird has been driven just over 14,500 miles. The listing doesn't state whether this is the mileage on the chassis or on the V8 that was reinstalled in 2000. Not only is this an extraordinarily quick car, but Superbirds are super rare , as only 135 were ever built with the original 7.0-liter Hemi V8.

Before we dive too deep into the a few examples, though, can we just take a second to appreciate how perfectly Wired journalist Miles Klee summed up the Cybertruck's woes? It's beautiful:

Automotive industry observers were quick to surmise that the vehicle's weak sales, delayed deliveries, inflated pricing, numerous recalls, and connection to Musk's far-right MAGA politics may also have factored into the decision. Longtime detractors of the polarizing steel-paneled truck, originally positioned as an electric rival to classic gas-powered pickups, jeered Musk and Tesla fans over its demise, noting with some pleasure that the Cybertruck would exit the market within four years of its November 2023 rollout.

I don't get the feeling he's one of those Cybertruck fans left brokenhearted following the cancellation announcement, which is good. Miles gets an invite to my upcoming Cybertruck Is Dead cookout next year. Anyway, onto the schadenfreude. Here's a thread he found from a Cybertruck owners' forum that you'll definitely want to scroll through. "Worst possible news," one poster wrote, adding, "No chance to buy another in future years for a newer model or after a car accident. No more aftermarket mods. No more service or parts."

In addition to highlighting a few of the best sad reactions, Wired also spoke with Cybertruck fans to hear their thoughts directly. "So everybody in my group, they are not happy," a contractor in Palm Springs name Michael Goldman told Wired . "I've had people reaching out to me through the group, asking me, like, 'What are you going to do?' And I'm like, 'Dude, I don't know.'" That group, by the way, is called Cybertruck Owners Only and has more than 82,000 members, every single one of whom we can assume is equally depressed now.

The article also uses the "betrayal" and "disappointment" to describe how many owners feel, which always feels good to see. As for Goldman, he told Wired he nearly bought a second Cybertruck to have for when his first one dies. Unfortunately for Mr. Goldman here, that didn't work out because Tesla pulled the ultimate Tesla move on him right before he pulled the trigger. "I'll be honest with you, I was going pull the trigger on a [Cyberbeast] about two days ago, and I have a reservation already in my phone," Goldman told Klee. But before he officially put his order in, "the price increased like another $8,000 or something, and that was my sign to not do it."

That price increase wasn't personal, though. Per Car and Driver , while the Cybertruck will reportedly stay in production through some point in 2027, the only version you can now buy costs $112,000. So that's not exactly cheap. Then again, who expects consistent pricing out of Tesla? You may not have to negotiate with a dealer salesperson, but Tesla pricing is still an expensive game of Russian roulette, and it has been for years.

Speaking with Wired , Troy Meekhof (the man behind the Cybertruck Guy Twitter account) said, "I absolutely do think this is the wrong move for the Tesla brand, and it's not necessarily because of the removal of an under-performing product, but it's a clear symbol of Tesla's aggression towards transitioning to autonomous vehicles only," adding, "If you ask me, it is far too aggressive, and I have a growing conviction that, at least in America, the population and legislators are not ready nor interested in autonomous vehicles today en masse." Huh.

raw_title: Rimac Is Ending Nevera Production With Just 71 Units Built
title: Rimac Is Ending Nevera Production With Just 71 Units Built
raw_summary: Rimac is wrapping up production of its all-electric Nevera hypercar with just 71 units finding homes. This is less than half of the 150 examples that Rimac initially planned to sell. It shows that, despite the Nevera delivering record-breaking levels of performance, demand for electric powertrains in the upper echelons of the hypercar market has fallen. However, Mate Rimac doesn't think the Nevera has been a failure. In a recent Instagram video, the company's founder revealed that Nevera production will end with 51 examples of the regular model sold and a further 20 Nevera R models finding customers. Though that's less than the 150 the Croatian company had expected to build, the Nevera is still the highest-selling electric hypercar of its kind. Until the new Tesla Roadster actually reaches the road, the Nevera will remain among the quickest, too.

In a recent Instagram video, the company's founder revealed that Nevera production will end with 51 examples of the regular model sold and a further 20 Nevera R models finding customers. Though that's less than the 150 the Croatian company had expected to build, the Nevera is still the highest-selling electric hypercar of its kind. Until the new Tesla Roadster actually reaches the road, the Nevera will remain among the quickest, too.

Eighteen months ago , Rimac set 24 world records in a single day with the Nevera R. This included a 0-400-0 kph (0-249-0 mph) record of just 25.79 seconds, a time that has since been beaten by the Koenigsegg Jesko Absolut. Last year, the Nevera R also set a 0-100 mph (160 kph) record of just 2.96 seconds, reached 124 mph (200 kph) in 3.95 seconds, and passed 186 mph (300 kph) in 7.89 seconds. The car was also pushed to an impressive top speed of 268.2 mph (431.45 kph), which had been an EV record until the BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme came along .

As staggeringly quick as the Nevera is, Rimac has had trouble selling all of the units it hoped to build. When the Nevera was first unveiled in 2021, all-electric performance cars were all the rage, and it seemed they were the future of the industry. Italian design house Pininfarina even got involved, using the Nevera as the base for its Battista hypercar. However, customer sentiment has shifted in recent years, with high-end buyers now preferring analog performance cars with big, screaming engines, like those from Gordon Murray Automotive and Koenigsegg.

Mate Rimac has compared electric cars like the Nevera with smartwatches , noting they're more advanced than traditional timepieces, yet don't have the same cachet or value. In the years to come, he believes high-end cars will stick to combustion engines. This philosophy is exemplified by the Bugatti Tourbillon. When Mate Rimac was brought in to help Bugatti create a successor to the Chiron, the Nevera was supposed to serve as the basis for an all-electric Bugatti. However, the Croatian instead decided to turn the Tourbillon into a hybrid with a massive naturally aspirated 8.3-liter V16 from Cosworth. Without the Nevera, the VW Group may have never pursued a deal with Rimac, and the Tourbillon may have never been created. For it, and for its V16 to live, the world needed the Nevera.

title: 2027 Aston Martin Valhalla
raw_summary: As with the outrageous Aston Martin Valkyrie , the Valhalla is a race car for the road, drawing inspiration from Formula 1 and utilizing lightweight materials and active aerodynamics. The Aston's exterior boasts an exaggerated version of the company's trademark grille along with slippery bodywork. Its central tub is composed of carbon fiber, and the Valhalla's exotic nature is accentuated by dihedral doors. Power comes from a Mercedes-AMG –sourced twin-turbo V-8, mated to a plug-in hybrid system that generates a combined 1064 horsepower. The gas engine feeds power to the rear tires, while the front tires are powered by a pair of electric motors. Aston estimates a top speed of 217 mph, and we think the Valhalla will get to 60 mph in the low-2.0-second range. The Valhalla also has an EV mode, which is good for around 6 miles of all-electric range. The Valhalla is a new model in Aston Martin's lineup, and it reaches the U.S. as a 2026 model.

The Valhalla is motivated by a massively powerful plug-in hybrid powertrain. At its core is a Mercedes-AMG–sourced twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crank. It feeds the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and apportions torque via an electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential. Additionally, two electric motors power the front wheels and a third is integrated into the transmission. Combined output is 1064 horsepower. Reversing is handled electrically. Lightweight carbon fiber makes up the car's core structure. The Valhalla also features F1-style pushrod front and multi-link rear suspensions with adaptive dampers; carbon-ceramic brakes are standard. Active aerodynamics are a major feature of the Valhalla, with movable front and rear wings that adjust to balance downforce and drag, maximize grip, and improve braking performance. When we drove the Valhalla , we found it to be remarkably engaging to drive for such a powerful, high-tech machine, and it's more friendly on the road than you'd expect, too.

Aston Martin claims that its "ultimate driver's supercar" is capable of reaching 62 mph from a standstill in 2.5 seconds. Given the Valhalla's massive power and all-wheel-drive system, we expect it to be considerably quicker than that. We'll know when we can put our test equipment on one of these rare beasts, and we will update this story with the results.

We estimate the Valhalla to offer an EPA combined fuel-economy rating of around 16 mpg. As a plug-in hybrid, it will have a short EV-only driving range of around 6 miles when the battery is fully charged.

The Valhalla's interior deftly blends form and function. It features extensive use of carbon fiber, giving the cabin a unique visual character while keeping weight to a minimum. Sitting front and center before the driver is a rectangular F1-inspired steering wheel that features physical infotainment controls. Forward of the steering wheel is a column-mounted digital display that shows a linear tachometer in Race mode and a speedometer and navigation information during road driving. A carbon brace runs the width of the cabin, on top of which floats a central infotainment screen that displays vital vehicle information, including battery charge level and energy-deployment data. The driver and passenger sit low in single-piece carbon-fiber seats. Be sure to pack light: the Valhalla does not have a trunk or a luggage compartment of any kind.

title: 2028 Ford Mustang Cobra with a Race Car-Derived V-8 Is Worth Waiting For
raw_summary: Ford only just launched the Mustang Dark Horse SC earlier this year, but the Blue Oval brand isn’t letting up when it comes to high-performance versions of its iconic pony car. While the S650-generation Mustang introduced the new Dark Horse branding—at the expense of the legendary Shelby nameplate—and saw the arrival of the new $300,000-plus GTD , Ford’s upcoming Mustang variant revives a famous name from the past: Cobra. The new Mustang Cobra is expected to slot between the Dark Horse and Dark Horse SC as an indirect successor to the last Shelby GT350 , providing track-ready performance and high-fidelity driver engagement. The Shelby GT350, offered from 2015–2020, is considered one of the best Mustangs ever, thanks to its naturally aspirated flat-plane-crank 5.2-liter V-8 known as Voodoo. The last Cobra is also coveted by Mustang fans, so the new track-focused model has big shoes to fill. And with a new engine most likely under the Cobra’s hood, there’s potential for another legendary Mustang to be born.

The Cobra will continue to utilize the S650 platform, itself an evolution of the S550 chassis that underpinned the Mustang from 2015–2023. The Cobra will adapt the Mustang into a dedicated track car, and we think it will also spawn a more hardcore Cobra R with even more extreme aerodynamics, stronger brakes, and greater weight savings, potentially even removing the backseat. We expect the Cobra’s bodywork to be based on the Dark Horse SC, but with small tweaks and possibly a rear wing that harkens back to the 2000 Cobra R .

Mustang fans are obviously clamoring for the return of the Voodoo, but we don’t think that’s what Ford has in store. Fret not, however, because the automaker is cooking up something special for the new Cobra.

Instead of the 5.2-liter Voodoo, the new Cobra will pack a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter engine derived from the Mustang GT3 race car that has triumphed at the 24 Hours of Daytona and secured a podium at Le Mans. The Coyote-based GT3 engine features a cross-plane crank, but the teaser video released by Ford emitted a high-revving scream, so there’s a chance that the Cobra’s engine will switch to a flat-plane-crank setup. Still, if you’ve recently been to an IMSA race, you’ll know the GT3 car produces a thunderous soundtrack, so enthusiasts are in for an auditory treat regardless.

Although Ford hasn’t confirmed that the Cobra will adapt the GT3 race car’s engine, in the first teaser it said the car would pack a “heart born from racing.” We don’t expect the Cobra to come close to the Dark Horse SC or GTD in terms of power, but we wouldn’t be shocked if the 5.4-liter V-8 exceeds the 550 horsepower that the GT3 car is restricted to by racing regulations.

title: Blazing Phoenix Yellow Adorns 2027 Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition
raw_summary: Acura is leaning on its heritage quite hard for 2027. It's celebrating the 30th anniversary of the DC2 Integra Type R by releasing a new low-production Heritage Edition. On top of that, the regular Type S gets plenty of new standard features. Let's break down everything Acura is giving the Integra for 2027, what fans might still miss, and where you can see this car starting this weekend. "The original Integra Type R became an icon because it delivered an exhilarating yet attainable, and unmistakably Acura performance experience, and the Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition is an incredible way to honor that legacy," said Mamadou Diallo, executive vice president of the Auto Business Center at American Honda Motor Co., Inc.

"The original Integra Type R became an icon because it delivered an exhilarating yet attainable, and unmistakably Acura performance experience, and the Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition is an incredible way to honor that legacy," said Mamadou Diallo, executive vice president of the Auto Business Center at American Honda Motor Co., Inc.

"For 2027, we're taking the Integra Type S even further with refreshed styling and more standard features, enhancing the experience of driving the most powerful, best-performing Integra ever." That refreshed styling is where we'll start because it's the most notable thing across the model-year changes.

The 2027 Integra Type S gets gloss black wheels, gloss black mirror caps, and yellow Brembo brake calipers on the outside. In the cabin, buyers will find quite a lot of dark grey now. It's on the shifter, the door trim, the instrument cluster, and even the door handles themselves. Acura offers a few different upholstery options, and each one is updated with new contrasting stripe accents. Those who pick the Ebony upholstery also get contrasting yellow accents. All cars get gloss black climate control knobs moving forward.

There are a few technical changes to consider as well. Memory brake hold makes its debut on the car as does a driver memory seat. When drivers go into reverse, the Integra can now tilt its wing mirrors down automatically to make parking a bit easier on the street. The Heritage Edition goes a little bit further and gets a bit weird. Let's break down the new stuff and how it does or doesn't link back to the DC2 that it's supposed to celebrate.

First, it gets an exclusive new color called Blazing Phoenix Yellow. It's not the same as the original "Phoenix Yellow" that was on the DC2, but Acura calls it a "more vibrant, modern interpretation of Phoenix Yellow." Interestingly, "Phoenix Yellow" wasn't actually available on the car from 30 years ago. It wasn't until 2000 that Acura introduced it, so... that's a touch awkward. The shift knob in the new car is titanium, which is both cool because of the metal itself and because the DC2 Type R had the same thing. What the DC2 didn't have were copper-finished wheels. That seems to be just a styling choice.

That all said, from a styling perspective, there's not a ton here that actually connects the cars. The DC2 Type R was a light two-door sports car, not a heavy four-door sedan . Outside of the badging, there's very little that actually ties these cars together from a design language standpoint.

Acura says the new Integra Type S starts at $55,995. The Heritage Edition, limited to just 700 examples, starts at $58,295. Those prices include a $1,395 destination charge. Perhaps most disappointingly, there are no performance improvements to the car for the new year.

raw_title: More Bugatti Customers Should Spec Polished Engine Covers, But They're All Too Chicken
title: More Bugatti Customers Should Spec Polished Engine Covers, But They're All Too Chicken
raw_summary: When you're buying a multi-million-dollar hypercar like a Bugatti Mistral , there are countless options to choose from even before you start getting into the really bespoke stuff . Selecting your paint shade, upholstery scheme, wheel design and stitching color is just the tip of the iceberg — for instance, on the Mistral, you can replace the elephant sculpture in the shifter with something else, like a mini Statue of Liberty or a screw from a 100-year-old Bugatti, as two customers have done. There is one option that only a tiny handful of Bugatti owners have gone for, and it's a real shame: the polished engine covers. Almost every modern Bugatti since the Veyron has had their engine bays exposed to the elements, and many buyers get the W16's engine covers painted in a matching or contrasting color, or maybe one of a dozen carbon-fiber finishes, instead of the regular gunmetal. The polished aluminum option is very expensive, but that's not what deters Bugatti customers from optioning it. No, they're just too wimpy.

article_paragraphs: When you're buying a multi-million-dollar hypercar like a Bugatti Mistral , there are countless options to choose from even before you start getting into the really bespoke stuff . Selecting your paint shade, upholstery scheme, wheel design and stitching color is just the tip of the iceberg — for instance, on the Mistral, you can replace the elephant sculpture in the shifter with something else, like a mini Statue of Liberty or a screw from a 100-year-old Bugatti, as two customers have done.

There is one option that only a tiny handful of Bugatti owners have gone for, and it's a real shame: the polished engine covers. Almost every modern Bugatti since the Veyron has had their engine bays exposed to the elements, and many buyers get the W16's engine covers painted in a matching or contrasting color, or maybe one of a dozen carbon-fiber finishes, instead of the regular gunmetal. The polished aluminum option is very expensive, but that's not what deters Bugatti customers from optioning it. No, they're just too wimpy.

This is a take I've freely said for a long time now, but it came to the forefront of my mind when I was at the 2026 Las Vegas Concours a couple weekends ago. While there wasn't a lineup of 47 Veyrons like last year , there were 20 modern Bugattis on display, including the Mistral you see here that has the polished engine covers on its W16 . I'm not usually one to gush over black cars but it's a pretty nice spec, and those magnesium wheels are another rare option.

The engine covers, though! Aren't they fantastic? That's how they look on a cloudy day, too, and are eye-catching even from a lower angle like that. Despite looking so awesome, fewer than 5% of buyers have gone for the option, and Bugatti's designers have told me it's because they don't want the covers to get dirty and scratched. I think that's exactly why more people should get them! Who doesn't love a bit of patina on a high-end car? Just look at the photos of this 2022 Chiron Super Sport that sold on Bring a Trailer last year. Isn't it neat to see the bright, shiny engine covers all scuffed up?

It's hard to pin down Bugatti option prices, but looking at the Monroneys (auto nerd speak for window sticker) of other Chiron sale listings helps. On a 2022 Chiron Pur Sport getting the engine covers painted in bright Tangerine cost $8,800, while going for an exposed carbon-fiber finish, like the one you see above, was $12,500. The polished option? $40,700.

OK, yeah, that's a lot. I know you can afford it, though, because you're buying a Bugatti, and in the grand scheme of things, it's not even really expensive. The Chiron's Sky View roof, for instance, was $62,000, and going for an exposed carbon-fiber body would've set you back at least $300,000. So what's an extra forty grand to get such a gorgeous engine bay? We don't yet know whether the Tourbillon's V16 will offer a similar finish (we know it'll have a carbon engine bay option), but I hope it does — and hopefully a much larger percentage of the 250 buyers will go for it.

article_paragraphs: Stellantis is playing another round of musical chairs with its executive team. This time, most of the changes stem from Bob Broderdorf’s return to the company. Broderdorf took medical leave from his position as Jeep’s CEO in August. He was replaced by Branden Coté, who retains his position as head of Jeep .

When Broderdorf’s departure from Jeep was announced, Stellantis had said he would come back in a different leadership role. Now off medical leave, Broderdorf will return to CEO status, this time as head of Dodge.

This isn’t Broderdorf’s first time at Dodge. He’s held seven different positions related to marketing, sales, product planning, and operations throughout his 25-year tenure at Stellantis. Dodge has been led by Matt McAlear since 2024, but McAlear has been spread thin at Stellantis since February, when he took over as Chrysler’s CEO and head of Alfa Romeo North America. McAleer will now focus solely on Chrysler, which is expected to release three new models in the next few years.

Chrysler’s lineup currently consists of just the Pacifica minivan. However, the brand has already announced the Airflow , a new compact SUV slated to launch in 2028 and start at less than $40,000, and is also working on the Arrow and Arrow Cross , which will come in under $30,000. Both CEOs will report to Tim Kuniskis, who assumes a new role as U.S. chief commercial officer. Kuniskis joined Stellantis in 1992 and served in several leadership roles before retiring from his position as head of Dodge and Ram in May 2024.

Retirement only lasted about seven months, though, and Kuniskis reportedly said he was “bored to death” after about two weeks out of work. By December 2024, Stellantis had announced Kuniskis’s appointment as Ram’s CEO . Since his return, Kuniskis has passed the Ram brand to Matt VanDyke and has taken over as head of American Brands, North America Marketing, SRT, and Stellantis’s Direct Connection parts division.

Now, Kuniskis adds U.S. retail, fleet sales, and the dealer network to his long list of leadership divisions following the departure of Michael Orange, former senior vice president of U.S. sales and network performance. Kuniskis will report to Stellantis North America’s chief operating officer, Pablo Di Si, who was appointed to the role earlier this month.

Di Si said in a press release that the leadership moves create a “clear line of decision-making” across the organization, which he says is important as Stellantis works to reach targets outlined in its FaSTLAne 2030 growth plan.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."

raw_summary: In the world of supersport bikes, few models are as iconic as Honda's Fireblade . article_paragraphs: In the world of supersport bikes, few models are as iconic as Honda's Fireblade . All versions of the 2027 CBR1000RR-R, including the standard Fireblade, Fireblade SP, and the Fireblade HRC Works Edition, run a 999 cc naturally aspirated inline-four with 214 horsepower at 14,000 rpm and 84.1 pound-feet of torque at 10,500 rpm. A two-piece intake funnel adjusts the length and diameter of the intake passage depending on vehicle speed, improving power at lower revs. Honda has also improved the bike's throttle-by-wire system for greater response and engine braking.

Honda says roughly 75% of all the CBR1000RR-R's parts have been redesigned for 2027. A new twin-tube aluminum frame sits at the heart of the bike, and the engine cylinder hangers have been improved to retain the same level of torsional rigidity as the old bike, but reduced lateral rigidity by 20%. Honda says this improves cornering performance, which is exactly what you want when riding a bike that's as track-focused as this.

Engineers have also developed a new swingarm for the Fireblade models that reduces lateral rigidity to improve tire feel. Optimizations have been made to the Showa suspension of the standard Fireblade and the electronically controlled Öhlins suspension of the SP version. A highlight of the updated Fireblade is a lightweight titanium fuel tank that includes an area of exposed titanium, perfect so you can flex on your mates who ride a Kawasaki , Suzuki, or a BMW.

Sitting at the top of the new CBR1000RR-R family is the HRC Works Edition that's essentially as close to a genuine World Superbike as regular folks can get. It comes standard with mechanically adjustable Öhlins NPX front forks and TTX36 rear suspension, in addition to the latest Brembo Hypure Sports brake components.

The track-ready HRC Works Edition is further bolstered by carbon fiber front winglets, a carbon front fender, and a carbon rear fairing. Buyers can also order this version with an HRC Racing Kit that adds a bottom-neutral shift system, head pipe collar, swingarm pivot collar, and PFM-FI and ignition system. If you want the HRC Works Edition, you'd better like red, as that's the only color it'll be sold in. It's also a strict single-seater, so buyers will need to leave their partner at home. The base CBR1000RR-R is the lightest of the trio, weighing in at a claimed 438.7 pounds, while the Fireblade SP is 443.1 lbs, and the HRC Works Edition weighs 440.9 lbs.

title: Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on the SSP
raw_summary: After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform. As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
summary: After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform. As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
article_paragraphs: After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer said in the memo reviewed by Reuters . The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.
Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer announced earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.
Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.
According to Autocar , Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

article_paragraphs: Deputies called off the chase, but a drone never lost sight of him.

For a brief moment last month, the 21-year-old driver of a bright blue Porsche 911 GT3 in Washington may have thought he could successfully flee from the police . However, he quickly discovered the law will always catch up, in what seems to be yet another case of someone with more money than sense.

This 21-year-old's brush with the law came on October 18 when police spotted him driving the Porsche recklessly on northbound Interstate 5, according to the Snohomish County Sheriff's Office . Deputies gave chase but called it off when the driver kept speeding through downtown Everett. The driver may have thought this was his moment to escape, but police kept him in view from the sky, and soon two deputies on the ground gave chase again. They deployed a set of spike strips, forcing the young driver to stop in the middle of the road and surrender.

Dramatic bodycam footage from the deputies captured the moment they arrested the man after a patrol car bumped the rear of the Porsche. As he was being read his Miranda rights, it appears the reality of what had happened finally began to dawn on the 21-year-old. He can be heard bursting into tears while being marched to the police cruiser.

Police later informed him that they would seize his car. He hilariously asked if there was any way he would be able to get the GT3 back, to which the officer responded, "Not run from the police." That's pretty apt advice if you ask us, as running from the police seems to have only worsened the situation . If he had pulled over when police first spotted him driving recklessly, he would have faced only a reckless driving charge. By choosing to flee, he ended up having his car seized and spent the night in jail.

Local authorities used the chase and arrest to remind drivers of the dangers of reckless driving, particularly speeding . Last year, 659 people died on Washington roads, according to data from the Washington Traffic Safety Commission , and 189 of these were killed in crashes involving speeding drivers. If you own a car like a Porsche 911 GT3, you should have the money for a track day, as a racetrack is the only safe place to push one to its limits.

raw_summary: Theon Design has established itself as one of the most recognizable names in the Porsche 911 restomodding scene, and its latest creation might just be the most impressive it's built to date. This stunning, one-off commission perfectly combines new materials, an updated design, and a serious powertrain and chassis setup to create what looks like the ultimate driver's car. Like other projects from Theon Design , this one started with a 964-generation 911 getting stripped back to its bare shell, and then custom carbon fiber body panels were fitted. Like other projects from Theon Design , this one started with a 964-generation 911 getting stripped back to its bare shell, and then custom carbon fiber body panels were fitted. These new carbon panels strip away roughly 661 lbs (300 kg) from the car and have been painted in a lovely shade of Oak Green Neo Metallic, which is inspired by Porsche's own shade of Oak Green Metallic. Making the car stand out further are a champagne-colored Porsche script and matching 17-inch champagne wheels and brake calipers.

Unlike some others in this field, such as Gunther Werks , Theon Design hasn't chased modern supercar power figures with its reborn 911. It uses a modified naturally aspirated 4.0-liter air-cooled flat-six with 419 horsepower and 322 pound-feet of torque. Those are some serious figures considering the car only weighs 2,535 lbs (1,150 kg). Modern conveniences like drive-by-wire and selectable engine maps have also been added. The engine operates alongside a five-speed manual transmission driving the rear wheels. It also rocks brake discs and calipers from a 993-generation Carrera RS.

Theon Design's upgrades don't stop with fresh bodywork, paint, and an upgraded engine. This car, like all its others, features an overhauled chassis that comes with semi-active TracTive dampers with custom spring rates designed specifically for British roads. It's also been fitted with Michelin Pilot Sport tires with tall sidewalls to boost ride quality.

The interior is also rather special. A set of Recaro CS seats is now fitted up front and wrapped in lovely light-brown leather. This leather continues across the rear seats, door panels, the transmission tunnel, and the lower half of the dashboard. Other surfaces are wrapped in black leather with brown contrast stitching. Theon's attention to detail extends to milled aluminum window switches, a modern climate-control system, and a custom wiring loom that alone saves 55 lbs (25 kg). Unlike a current 911, there are no screens in sight, as this car is all about delivering the purest expression of driving possible.

The British firm will soon have a special 911-based model that's even more exhilarating than this one promises to be. It's working on a new R-branded lineup where models will use a 4.0-liter flat-six with over 500 hp. These models will also go on an even stricter diet and weigh less than 2,200 lbs (1,000 kg). Prices for a 'basic' model like this Oak Green Neo Metallic car start at £435,000 ($576,000).

article_paragraphs: Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.
Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator shows today with a Los Angeles delivery address:

A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

On November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor . That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.
New inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search showed no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

If there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

article_paragraphs: Rimac is ending production of its all-electric Nevera hypercar at the end of 2026, Germany’s Auto Motor und Sport reports . And somewhat surprisingly, the same report suggests that just 71 of 190 planned Reveras were built over the course of its production run.

The base Nevera, and its later Nevera R variant, have held a number of records, including the title of world’s quickest car , what was once the EV lap record at the Nürburgring Nordschleife, and a quarter-mile run under 7.9 seconds . Those numbers may not have been enough to make the model a hit with buyers, though. According to the report, 51 of a planned 150 base-model Neveras were built, and 20 out of a planned 40 Nevera Rs reached production.

While the apparent final tally of Nevera production is striking, it is part of a larger pattern of electric hypercars failing to find an audience. The Lotus Evija once competed directly with Rimac’s Nevera, but Lotus has since moved on to a hybrid supercar with V-8 power. Former Rimac stakeholder Porsche once considered its own electric hypercar, only to pivot to an internal-combustion supercar instead. Even as cars like the Tesla Roadster and Yangwang U9 Xtreme make headlines with record-setting stunts, there are questions on whether or not a conventional hypercar buyer would be interested in paying for an EV.

Whether or not the Nevera itself was a success, the halo car did succeed in raising Rimac’s profile. Namesake founder Mate Rimac is now fully in charge of Bugatti, and Rimac Technology provides electric powertrain components to major cars like the Porsche 911 Turbo S. As the most significant electric hypercar to reach the market to date—well, perhaps along with the closely related Pininfarina Battista —the few Neveras in private hands represent a major leap forward for both electric performance and the Rimac brand itself.

Fred Smith's love of cars comes from his fascination with auto racing. Unfortunately, that passion led him to daily drive a high-mileage, first-year Porsche Panamera. He is still thinking about the last lap of the 2011 Indianapolis 500.

Let's start with the Honda Vezel e:HEV TrailSport, which is a new addition to the lineup and a follow-up to the TrailSport HRC concept from the Tokyo Auto Salon. The model introduces the rugged treatment to the Fit-based SUV, taking it further than the previously available Active Style accessory package .

The highlight of the exterior is the unique grille with a pair of LEDs looking like position lights. These are combined with orange accents on the fog light garnish and the top end of the grille, black roof rails, and an optional matte black sticker on the hood.

The TrailSport has a dark-themed interior with contrasting orange stitching and matching seatbelts. The seats combine synthetic leather upholstery with fabric inserts featuring special embroidery and a water-repellent coating. Standard equipment includes a heated steering wheel, blind spot monitoring, and a power tailgate, although the 9-inch infotainment, the wireless charging pad, and the multi-view camera are available as options.

The flagship variant of the Japanese-spec Honda Vezel is the updated e:HEV RS, building on the sporty trim unveiled after the facelift of 2025 . The small SUV retains the dark chrome aero kit of its predecessor, but the 18-inch alloy wheels are now finished in matte black. These are combined with black chrome Honda emblems and a red RS badge mounted on the grille.
Honda has confirmed that the RS-specific lowered suspension and the sharper steering setup are also carried over, promising improved handling compared to the rest of the Vezel lineup.

Moving inside, we find black synthetic leather upholstery with suede inserts on the seats, red and white stitching and piping, a dark headliner, and stainless steel sports pedals. Equipment is even more generous, with the 9-inch touchscreen and wireless charging fitted as standard, although the multi-view system and the premium audio remain optional.

While the regular Vezel is available with gasoline and hybrid powertrain options, the TrailSport and the RS can only be ordered with the standard 1.5-liter e:HEV setup, which is good for 129 hp (96 kW / 131 PS) and 253 Nm (186 lb-ft).

title: The surprising convergence behind F1's increasingly competitive 2026 season
raw_summary: As George Russell took pole for F1 2026's curtain raiser in Australia by a whopping eight tenths over Mercedes's nearest rivals, you could see the collective heads drop in the paddock. article_paragraphs: As George Russell took pole for F1 2026's curtain raiser in Australia by a whopping eight tenths over Mercedes's nearest rivals, you could see the collective heads drop in the paddock.

With this season the first year of all-new regulations, both on the chassis and power unit side, there were genuine fears of a 2014 repeat, with Mercedes out in front and the competition fighting over scraps.

Mercedes certainly did try to make the most of its early advantage, despite its power unit's reliability woes, as it has now sealed both the drivers' and constructors' title with three rounds to spare.

But the second half of the season after the summer break paints a different competitive picture. A picture in which all four top teams have had their chance to shine, owing to the ebb and flow of powerful upgrades being fast-tracked as part of a frantic in-season development race.

Lando Norris dominated either side of the summer break with wins in Hungary and the Netherlands, and what should have been a third win in Madrid. That followed a strong spell for Ferrari with one win apiece for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc .
Later on, Red Bull made perhaps the most impressive comeback of all by clawing back one second, enabling Max Verstappen to take three wins over the past five races.

The end result is that Mercedes outscored Red Bull by just a single point since the summer break, while Ferrari could have been closer with better race weekend execution. McLaren has firmly been the fourth-fastest team only for Norris to excel in the wet in Sao Paulo last week.

That convergence is best observed in qualifying, with the top four teams covered by three tenths in Singapore and Mexico. Austin was a difficult race for McLaren, but Kimi Antonelli , Verstappen and Leclerc all qualified within 0.230s at COTA. The absolute highlight was a thrilling qualifying session at the inaugural edition of Madring's Spanish Grand Prix, where the top five qualified within 0.195s across four different teams.

title: Mercedes Stops Investment In German Factories And Weighs Plant Closures
raw_summary: Mercedes-Benz has issued an alarming statement as it fights to cut costs amid rising industry pressure. The German automaker announced that it will stop all investment in passenger car manufacturing in its home country of Germany. The company also stated that plant closures may be possible, as profits continue to be squeezed, with production potentially being shifted to Hungary. The announcement is in direct response to a disagreement with its workers' unions, as the company attempts to improve profitability by reducing labor costs across its German factories. The news was broken on Thursday, when an interview with members of the Mercedes-Benz board was released internally. According to a report from the Financial Times , production head Michael Schiebe said that "the current cost structures do not allow us to invest in Germany."

article_paragraphs: Mercedes-Benz has issued an alarming statement as it fights to cut costs amid rising industry pressure. The German automaker announced that it will stop all investment in passenger car manufacturing in its home country of Germany. The company also stated that plant closures may be possible, as profits continue to be squeezed, with production potentially being shifted to Hungary.

The announcement is in direct response to a disagreement with its workers' unions, as the company attempts to improve profitability by reducing labor costs across its German factories. The news was broken on Thursday, when an interview with members of the Mercedes-Benz board was released internally. According to a report from the Financial Times , production head Michael Schiebe said that "the current cost structures do not allow us to invest in Germany."
The company is in the middle of ongoing negotiations with Germany's IG Metall union and the Mercedes General Works Council. The workers' unions have vowed to fight any potential closures.

Mercedes-Benz has asked its German plant employees to work for 40 hours a week without extra pay, which is five hours more than the standard for the German automotive sector. Their reasoning is that the labor costs associated with German plants are too high compared to those of Eastern Europe and the US.

Mercedes has been struggling with profitability of late, with expected returns to be just 2%-3% this year, compared to the double-digit projections that they had hoped for. The company made heavy investments in EVs, but adoption had been slower than expected in Europe and the US. Meanwhile, in the company's largest market, China, passenger car sales have continued to falter, with Chinese vehicle sales falling by 31% in the third quarter of 2026.

Mercedes isn't alone, with VW in similar financial trouble, last month pressing pause on ID Golf development. Labor costs in Germany are sometimes as much as five times higher than they would be at other plants in Eastern Europe. Mercedes-Benz already has a passenger vehicle manufacturing facility in Hungary, while outside of Europe it has plants in China, South Africa, and the U.S. Further local assembly JVs exist for complete knock-down vehicles in India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Vietnam.

Two German plants are apparently on the chopping block, according to earlier comments made by Michael Schiebe, Member of the Board of Management of Mercedes-Benz Group AG for Production, Quality & Supply Chain Management.

Currently, Mercedes-Benz operates three plants for assembling passenger vehicles in Germany. The largest is its Sindelfingen plant, which has 31,500 employees. Its Bremen plant has 10,500 employees, while the Rastatt plant provides jobs for 7,000 workers. The company also has 7 other German plants, including Untertürkheim (Stuttgart), Berlin, and Hamburg, which assemble drivetrains and components. Düsseldorf and Wörth handle commercial vehicles, while the Kamenz plant assembles lithium-ion batteries, and Affalterbach is home to AMG.

title: Florida Sinks SS United States In Gulf Of Mexico To Protect The Environment, And I'm Sorry, But That's Just Too Many Jokes
raw_summary: In a hilariously ironic turn of events, Okaloosa County, Florida , sank the SS United States to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico on Veteran's Day, turning it into the world's largest artificial reef to provide shelter for local marine life in the wake of human-caused coral reef decimation in the area. The SS United States is longer than the Titanic , measuring 990 feet from bow to stern and 17 stories in height. It was once the fastest ocean liner in the world, known for carrying royalty and celebrities between the U.S. and Europe from its maiden voyage in 1952 to its retirement in 1969. It actually still holds the record for the world's fastest trans-Atlantic ocean liner, accomplishing the trek in 3 days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes at an average speed of 35.59 knots, and it achieved top speeds of over 38.3 knots, or 44 mph, during trials. This serves as a reminder that even once-great nations — er, ships — can find themselves fallen so far from their former glory that they are better off being totally gutted and sank to the bottom of the ocean rather than wasting time and resources attempting to resuscitate them only for them to still be outdated and irrelevant in a modern world.

The SS United States was originally designed to be converted from luxury ocean liner to troop transport vessel in the event of war like the also-retired Queen Mary was, with the ability to carry 14,000 troops 10,000 miles without refueling, though the SS United States never actually faced wartime use. It was powered by four Westinghouse 1,000-psi steam turbines and eight boilers, which combined to produce a mind-boggling total power output of 240,000 horsepower.

Following the ship's retirement in 1969, the SS United States, "spent its years haunting old shipyards while failed plans to restore it came and went" according to Northeastern Global News . Okaloosa County bought the vessel in 2024 after it faced a court-ordered eviction from its prior docking point at Pier 82 along the Delaware River in South Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, where it stayed for nearly three decades.

Okaloosa County chose to sink the ship in its waters to attract tourism from divers, as its top funnels should be easily accessible at just 55 feet below the surface, while its keel will be at a depth of 180 feet. Prior to this, the largest artificial reef on the planet was the 910-foot-long USS Oriskany, which was a U.S. warship that was intentionally sunk in 2006. The SS United States Conservancy plans to commemorate the remarkable ship by constructing a museum and visitor's center in Florida.

Before we get into the details about the Heritage Edition, let’s talk about the changes Acura has made to the standard ‘27 Type S. Every example now features gloss-black 19-inch wheels and mirror caps, and the Brembo-branded brake calipers are now painted yellow. There are no powertrain changes, so a rowdy 320-hp 2.0-liter turbo four and sweet-shifting six-speed manual transmission still feed the front wheels.

Inside, Acura now makes the door-panel trim, door handles, and shift boot dark gray, and that applies to the dashboard too, which also adopts a new diamond pattern. The three knobs that control the climate settings are now all gloss black, and Acura says it has redesigned the upholstery options. The Red and Orchid (white) themes feature faux-suede accents that are black and blue, respectively, but the Ebony option features yellow stitching, which extends to the steering wheel, door panels, and shift boot. The driver’s seat now has memory settings, as does the brake-hold feature, and both exterior mirrors tilt down when the car is put into reverse.

If you missed your chance to buy a Phoenix Yellow Integra Type R back in the day, Acura is turning back the clock and giving you another shot. Sure, the new Type S model has an extra pair of doors and put on some weight, but it remains one of our favorite driver’s cars, and the Heritage Edition is the only way to get the new Blazing Phoenix Yellow paint job (at least for the ‘27 model year). Not only is the new retro-themed Type S the first Integra with yellow paint since the 2001 Type R, but it also features exclusive copper-colored wheels. Its interior color is limited to the black-and-yellow theme offered on other new Type S models, but the Heritage Edition alone has a titanium shift knob—same as the Honda Civic Type R .

title: VW Rebadges Chinese Van That Rivals Its Own Crafter
raw_summary: The Volkswagen Crafter might be competing with large vans such as the Ford Transit, Renault Trafic, Fiat Ducato, and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter in various markets around the world, but it is absent from South America. In order to fill that void, VW has unveiled the new Tempest, which is a rebadged version of the Chinese Maxus Deliver 9, also sold as the LDV Deliver 9 and Maxus V90 since 2019. Back to the large van, the VW Tempest retains the sheet metal of its LDV twin, but gains a redesigned nose. A slimmer black grille with the VW emblem connects the carry-over LED headlights, joined by a new cooling intake on the front bumper. The interior has also been carried over, including the 12-inch infotainment display and multiple storage solutions.

The LCV is available in Cargo, Window, Minibus, and Truck body style variants with two different heights. Despite the similarities with its Chinese twin, VW claims that its own engineering team carried out over 250 technical modifications, adapted over 50 manufacturing processes, and completed 1.5 million km (932,000 miles) of testing during development.

Under the hood of the VW Tempest lies a SAIC-sourced 2.0-liter four-cylinder turbodiesel producing 174 hp (130 kW / 176 PS) and 400 Nm (295 lb-ft) of torque. The extra power and torque compared to the LDV donor vehicle were made possible thanks to performance modifications specific to the Brazilian market. The mill is exclusively mated to a six-speed manual gearbox, moving rear wheels.

Depending on the variant, cargo volume ranges between 9.7-12.3 cubic meters (343-434 cubic feet). For comparison, the global-spec VW Crafter can carry anywhere between 9.3 and 18.4 cubic meters (328-650 cubic feet).

While the VW Tempest has just been unveiled, the automaker announced it has already received over 1,000 pre-orders from Brazilian customers. Pricing has yet to be announced. The company has also confirmed that availability of the van will expand to Argentina early next year. The model is manufactured in SAIC facilities in China.

It is worth noting that the LDV Deliver 9 is a direct rival to VW's own-developed Crafter in regions like Australia, New Zealand, Europe, and the UK, where both models are being sold simultaneously. Still, badge engineering is a common strategy in trucks and LCVs, with automakers trying their best to save valuable R&D resources through partnerships, while covering a large portion of the market.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet , showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

The new S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

The other big piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

Perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.
Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):

When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February , it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.
And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.
Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.
If you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

title: Europe's Hydrogen Strategy Should Begin With the Industrial Customer
raw_summary: A European fertiliser manufacturer buys ammonia. Its immediate concern is getting the right product, at the right quality and price, with reliable deliveries. The manufacturer may produce ammonia using hydrogen made on its own site, buy hydrogen through a pipeline, or import ammonia made somewhere else. The last choice preserves much of the downstream industrial work but creates no demand for additional hydrogen production or pipelines inside Europe. That distinction belongs at the start of Europe’s hydrogen strategy. The European Commission has reopened the strategy for consultation, with submissions due November 23. The Commission acknowledges that renewable and low-carbon hydrogen production and use have grown more slowly than expected. Europe’s public investment decisions now need a closer look at the industries expected to use hydrogen, the products they make, and the routes by which those products can be supplied competitively. The consultation is open until November 23, 2026.

article_paragraphs: A European fertiliser manufacturer buys ammonia. Its immediate concern is getting the right product, at the right quality and price, with reliable deliveries. The manufacturer may produce ammonia using hydrogen made on its own site, buy hydrogen through a pipeline, or import ammonia made somewhere else. The last choice preserves much of the downstream industrial work but creates no demand for additional hydrogen production or pipelines inside Europe. That distinction belongs at the start of Europe’s hydrogen strategy.

The European Commission has reopened the strategy for consultation, with submissions due November 23. The Commission acknowledges that renewable and low-carbon hydrogen production and use have grown more slowly than expected. Europe’s public investment decisions now need a closer look at the industries expected to use hydrogen, the products they make, and the routes by which those products can be supplied competitively. The consultation is open until November 23, 2026.
I submitted a demand-led assessment to the Commission on November 11. My TFIE Strategy Briefing explains the industrial argument, and the open research report documents the model and its assumptions.

Europe’s existing hydrogen market is primarily a market for industrial chemicals. ACER estimated EU consumption of about 7.4 million tons in 2024, including 4.2 million tons for petroleum refining and 1.9 million tons for ammonia. Passenger cars, building heat and power generation account for very little of that established market. Refining faces structural decline as petroleum demand changes, while fertiliser and chemical producers can keep manufacturing products even when some upstream inputs come from elsewhere.

Steelmaking also has choices that cannot be captured by a single hydrogen-demand target. Producers can use recycled scrap, purchase reduced iron made where electricity is cheaper, or use hydrogen-based direct reduction where its economics work. The equipment, feedstock quality and production location determine the actual hydrogen requirement. Industrial heat offers direct electrical options for many duties. Transport electrification cuts the amount of liquid fuel that must be produced in the first place. These choices determine hydrogen demand long before anyone chooses a pipeline route.

Electricity costs expose why the industrial comparison matters. Electrolysis consuming 55 kWh/kg uses €3.30 of electricity per kilogram at €60/MWh, and €5.50 at €100/MWh. Those prices exclude the electrolyser, finance, maintenance, compression and delivery. An industrial customer pays for the finished product, not for the complexity of the process used to manufacture it.

The new assessment compares qualifying green ammonia imported into Europe at modelled 2050 delivered costs of €755–839/t with European ammonia made using on-site hydrogen at about €1,222/t. The €383–467/t gap puts a substantial price on choosing the domestic route in this model. Emissions certification, quality, reliability and supply concentration belong in the procurement appraisal, alongside the cost and strategic value of retaining European upstream production. They do not turn a forecast of ammonia demand into a forecast of domestic hydrogen demand.

Industrial policy has reasons to support European production beyond the lowest immediate price. Domestic facilities provide employment, technical capabilities and supply security. The right decision is to identify those benefits, calculate the extra cost and state who will pay it. Hydrogen production quotas bury that choice in a volume target and risk making European industrial products less competitive.

raw_title: Comparison Test: 2026 Jeep Recon Moab vs. 2027 Rivian R2 Performance
title: Comparison Test: 2026 Jeep Recon Moab vs. 2027 Rivian R2 Performance
raw_summary: Normally, it’s easy to identify an incumbent. Establishment figures tend to enjoy advantages—experience, name recognition, resources—that are scarce for upstarts. But in the case of the 2027 Rivian R2 and the 2026 Jeep Recon Moab, it’s hard to say who’s the incumbent and who’s the challenger. Jeep has been building SUVs since the 1940s, as it’s happy to constantly remind you, but is relatively new to EVs. Meanwhile, the first Rivians hit the road just five years ago, but EVs are all that it builds, and the R2 is the brand’s third model. Which incumbency is more advantageous? Let’s take a look. The fresh-out-of-the-oven R2 hews to the typical launch strategy of offering the most expensive version first. Thus, our 2027 model is a Performance trim with the Launch package, which brings a 4400-pound tow rating and hands-free driving assist. Simpler variants are coming soon, priced closer to 50 grand, but our tester with its $2000 Launch Green paint tallied $61,485. Happily, the R2’s most delightful feature, its power roll-down hatch glass, is standard. Sorry, Toyota 4Runner , Rivian is onto the lifestyle appeal of a dropped rear window with a surfboard poking out. Or a dog or two who won’t be breathing exhaust fumes.
