Happily, the R2’s most delightful feature, its power roll-down hatch glass, is standard. Sorry, Toyota 4Runner , Rivian is onto the lifestyle appeal of a dropped rear window with a surfboard poking out. Or a dog or two who won’t be breathing exhaust fumes.
See all results for new 2026 Jeep Recon EV for sale near 51503

The Recon is so far only available in Moab trim, which at Jeep signifies elevated off-road capability along with an elevated price. Indeed, the Recon’s $68,990 base sticker exceeds the R2’s as-tested figure, and an assortment of goodies further inflated our as-tested price to $73,345. Major options included the $1995 Comfort package, which adds ventilated front seats and heated second-row seats, and the $995 towing package (max capacity: 3300 pounds). Plenty of off-road hardware is standard: skid plates, an electronically locking rear differential, and 33-inch all-terrain tires. And because Jeep is leaning into the “Wrangler, but electric” theme, the Recon’s doors and rear windows are removable without tools. But, at about 70 pounds each, the doors might not be removable without a daily swig of creatine.

The R2’s styling is “Honey, I Shrunk the R1.” It’s clean, modern, and employs the signature Rivian ovoid headlights. There’s nothing too revolutionary about it, but that works to its advantage—Rivian wants to sell the hell out of this thing, and divisive styling is not a smart play for conquesting market share from internal-combustion rivals. (Just ask the Tesla Cybertruck .) And, hey, you can’t go wrong with big wheels pushed out to the corners. Our tester had all-season tires on 21-inch wheels, the mall-crawler spec, but Rivian does offer tougher-looking 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires. Those, however, will drop EPA-rated range from 330 miles to 307 miles.
See all results for new 2026 Jeep Recon EV for sale near 51503

The Recon’s aesthetic is intentionally anti-EV, with nary a concession to aerodynamics or rolling resistance. It’s square, tall, and has a front bumper that looks like a bulldog’s underbite, all of which contributes to an atmosphere-battling 0.404 coefficient of drag. It doesn’t quite pull off the Wrangler’s studied minimalism, but the Recon is the most off-road-forward EV this side of a Hummer or a Mercedes-Benz G580e. It’s also capable of changing up its look, depending on whether the doors and windows are removed. Buttoned up, it’s a regular SUV with an off-road bent, but ditch the doors and open the full-length canvas roof, and it’s like you’re driving something from the car-stripping contest in I’m Gonna Git You Sucka .

Inside, the R2 and Recon represent their respective manufacturers’ design philosophies. Whether you prefer the spare, screen-centric Rivian or the more conventional Jeep is a matter of your priorities (and, maybe, age), but the Recon is undeniably more user-friendly. Stellantis may whipsaw on its product planning— EVs! No, V-8s! —but its interiors are consistently good, from Jeep to Ram to the Chrysler Pacifica . A splash of tan leather across the top of the steering wheel matches the seats, and a red panel on the console draws attention to the rocker switch for the terrain modes. Both the Rivian and Jeep feature large touchscreens, but the Recon augments its touchscreen functions with hard buttons (on both the dash and the steering wheel) and knobs for volume and tuning. The Jeep’s Uconnect 5 system also supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, while the Rivian doesn’t allow phone mirroring.

article_paragraphs: Months after patent drawings leaked online, Lucid dropped fresh teaser footage of its upcoming Cosmos EV

Lucid has dropped a new video that teases its upcoming entry-level Cosmos electric SUV ahead of the car's debut next year. The Cosmos is arguably the most important vehicle the American brand has designed to date and could be make-or-break for Lucid, given that it is still unprofitable after launching and selling the Air sedan and Gravity SUV.

In a promotional video shared on X, Lucid describes how it has "always looked at movement differently." It's a nice video, showcasing the brand's models in a host of different environments, including outdoors, on the beach, and in city centers. The clip then gets especially intriguing toward the end, where a camouflaged prototype of the Cosmos is showcased during winter testing in New Zealand. The video ends with clips previewing the front and rear of the vehicle.

As leaked patent images from earlier this year revealed, the Cosmos will follow a familiar design theme as the Air and Gravity, albeit in a slightly smaller package. The teaser shows a thin LED headlight with an intricate daytime running light pattern. Lucid has also previewed the SUV's rear, which includes an illuminated Lucid badge and narrow LED taillights.

The shape of the Cosmos's rear end somewhat reminds us of the Genesis GV60. Like that EV, the Cosmos has a small lip spoiler running across the rear and essentially splitting the rear window into two segments. Admittedly, the Lucid does appear longer than the GV60, and the roof seems to sit slightly more upright.

Lucid had originally intended to launch the Cosmos in late 2026, but in August, it confirmed the model won't hit the production line until the second half of 2027. It will be built at the company's AM2 facility in Saudi Arabia, rather than at the Arizona factory that currently builds the Air and Gravity models.

The Cosmos won't simply be a smaller version of the Gravity. Instead, it's going to be the first model underpinned by Lucid's new midsize platform that will also spawn a second EV known as the Earth. This platform will include a new electric drive unit called Atlas. It uses 30% fewer parts than the drive units featured in the Air and Gravity and will also be lighter and cheaper. The Cosmos is expected to initially hit the market with a 69-kWh battery and a targeted driving range of more than 300 miles, and a larger pack may be added in the future.

We've always looked at movement differently. From the calm of a well-crafted cabin to the ease of a journey and the thrill of acceleration, it's about elevating the experience of movement, mile after mile. article_paragraphs: Uber is notifying thousands of drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.

In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California , the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.
The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.

TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.
Online productivity startup Notion confirmed its data was also stolen in the Fireworks hack.

“The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch, deferring our questions to Fireworks.
Uber did not say how many customers are affected by the breach, nor how many drivers it was notifying about the incident.

When reached by email, a spokesperson for Fireworks confirmed that the company identified a security issue involving unauthorized access to some of its systems, which affected customer data, but the spokesperson did not address our questions about the incident.

title: Is Tesla The Apple Of The EV Industry?
raw_summary: Tesla is an interesting company at an interesting phase of the electric vehicle transition. Well, it has always been an interesting company in this transition. However, lately, as the industry has moved quickly into a new phase, I have been wondering where Tesla will sit amidst it in the coming years. However, lately, as the industry has moved quickly into a new phase, I have been wondering where Tesla will sit amidst it in the coming years.
article_paragraphs: Tesla is an interesting company at an interesting phase of the electric vehicle transition. Well, it has always been an interesting company in this transition. However, lately, as the industry has moved quickly into a new phase, I have been wondering where Tesla will sit amidst it in the coming years.

While there are now hundreds and hundreds of electric vehicle models on the market and EV share of new vehicle sales have risen to 32% globally (or 23% if we only count full electrics/BEVs) , Tesla sells only two models but remains the second best selling BEV producer in the world. It remains solidly ahead of other automakers and only trails Chinese giant BYD (or also Geely if we throw in PHEVs).
In the US, where there’s much less EV competition (especially because of Chinese EVs basically being blocked from entering the market), Tesla’s share of EV sales is above 50%.

The Apple iPhone holds about 20–22% of the global smartphone market, and around 58% of the US smartphone market. While that’s a bit higher than Tesla’s shares, it’s quite similar. And considering that Apple just sells that one phone (but in a few different versions) and Tesla just sells the Model 3 and Model Y, it’s hard to not see a comparison.

As EV sales have been picking up in parts of the world, or at least reaching portions of the market in the USA, it seems to me that a lot of people choose Tesla because they’ve heard it’s the EV brand. Tesla has long been the face of the EV transition in most of the world, and even considered the only “real” option. I know of many buyers in the US who just went straight to Tesla without looking at other options. It’s a bit like how many people will only consider and look at Apple for phones. However, how much will that change in the coming years? Will Tesla’s dominance fade further (it’s already down from about 80% of the market in the US to a bit more than 50%) as more and more options come to market, or will it hold it’s special position as a first mover, a tech leader, and an EV-only carmaker?

One more interesting issue here is the matter of “Full Self Driving” — which only comes as “Supervised” at the moment, but Tesla is itching to make a fully hands-off, eyes-off option for Tesla owners. Could Tesla achieve a leading role for years again of having the only fully hands-off, eyes-off, self-driving consumer cars on the road? Or is it not going to beat other automakers to market with a self-driving feature that takes liability for any accidents away from the human operating the car and allows them to sleep, watch movies, work, etc. in the car? This has been hotly debated for about a decade, with Tesla nearly a decade late on Elon Musk’s targets for this, but the company is now operating robotaxis in a few cities and ramping up production of the Cybercab. Risky or not, is Tesla close to taking on liability for humans using FSD in their own cars? And if it does take that step, will that make demand for Tesla cars so high that Tesla sees its EV market share increase significantly again?

I know many people have strong opinions on these matters — on both sides of the debate. Some are certain Tesla is going to rise again and will release true Full Self Driving broadly soon, or at least long before other automakers. Some are certain Tesla’s vision-only approach is fatally flawed and Tesla will never take on full liability for Tesla owners using FSD. I don’t have enough insight or expertise to say one thing is absolutely certain and the other is not, but I do think the FSD matter is quite important to Tesla remaining “the Apple of the EV industry” — even potentially without taking on accident liability. Even with things staying as they are, I wonder if Tesla could remain the dominant EV player in the US and some other markets just because of its early reputation, branding, and 21st century marketing. We shall see.

Spyker made a stunning return to the automotive world in August, unveiling its wild new C8 Preliator XXV Coupe during Monterey Car Week. article_paragraphs: After surviving two bankruptcies, boutique automaker Spyker is back with a stunning, hand-built supercar aimed directly at Pagani and Bugatti.

Spyker made a stunning return to the automotive world in August, unveiling its wild new C8 Preliator XXV Coupe during Monterey Car Week. The company's revival started in October 2025 when co-founder Victor Muller secured the rights to the firm's name after it went bankrupt for a second time in 2021. So, Spyker is back, and now it's aiming at the upper echelons of the market. Is Spyker's third time finally the charm?

In the early 2000s, the Dutch automaker found success selling its hand-built models, including the C8 Laviolette and C8 Spyder, using Audi-sourced V8 engines. Eager to expand its presence, Spyker acquired the Midland F1 team in 2006 and competed throughout the 2007 championship as Spyker F1. Its diversion into F1 wasn't a success. The same can be said about Spyker's purchase of Saab. Spyker secured an agreement with GM to purchase Saab for $394 million in 2010, but less than a year later, Saab's cash reserves ran dry and was forced to stop production and went bankrupt. Spyker itself fell into bankruptcy for the first time in 2014, and then again in 2021 after what seemed to be a promising resurgence.

In an exclusive interview with CarScoops, Muller has blamed the company's expansion into Formula 1 and its acquisition of Saab as the cause of its previous "setbacks." Now with a renewed focus on building limited-run, high-end automobiles, the company has seemingly rediscovered its mojo. It's returned at the perfect time.

Wealthy collectors and car enthusiasts are happily dropping millions of dollars on exclusive supercars and hypercars, unlike at any other time in the past, shunning EVs and demanding traditional driving thrills. Spyker has secured fresh funding for its rebirth and has already finalized engineering of the new C8 Preliator XXV Coupe . Deliveries will start in the second quarter of 2027. By the end of next year, all 25 units will have been built.

"We will position ourselves at the very top of the market, where Pagani, Koenigsegg, Bugatti, and Gordon Murray Automotive are the established brands," Muller told CarScoops. "We do not have to convince buyers that Spyker offers something genuinely different, because it already does. We have clearly set ourselves apart through our design, our attention to detail and the outstanding craftsmanship of our workforce. The brand's heritage, dating back to 1880, complements that picture."

Although there's plenty of competition in the high-end automotive space, Spyker is confident it can stand out. According to Muller, "there are only a handful of authentic hypercar brands that qualify as boutique brands: companies that have either been around for a very long time, such as Bugatti and Spyker, or were founded more recently, such as Pagani and Koenigsegg." According to him, "most others are not here to stay."

The Dutch company doesn't have ambitions to produce hundreds of vehicles. In fact, "Spyker will build 50 cars for the entire global market" in a good year, Muller told us, and it has more than enough willing buyers to sustain itself.

title: What's Your Weirdest Non-USDM Car Spotting Moment?
raw_summary: If you're like me, car spotting is worth getting excited about , especially when you see something that wasn't originally sold in your country. Maybe that last part is just me, but you get my point, and it's what brings me to today's question. I want to know what your weirdest non-U.S. domestic market car spotting moment is. What car that was never meant to be driven in the U.S. made you stop dead in your tracks and take a few photos when you saw one Stateside? The thing is, I'm not asking for the time you saw some sort of supercar over here that isn't technically sold in America. No, I'm looking for boring, strange and otherwise mundane cars that no one in their right mind would bring to America, but someone in their wrong mind did anyway.

The inspiration for this question is a vehicle I saw over four years ago and still think about almost every day. I couldn't tell you what I was doing in Bethesda, Maryland, at 10 a.m. on June 14, 2022, but it's a time and place that'll live in infamy, because that's where and when I saw an utterly unremarkable Škoda Roomster traveling along one of Maryland's many roads. Other than the fact its standard Virginia license plate was zip-tied onto the European license plate bracket, there was nothing about this Roomster that would give away that it was something weird to the uninitiated.

It's one of the few times I've ever pulled my phone out while driving, because I almost couldn't believe what I was seeing. It's not like Škodas are even sold in Mexico or Canada. Whoever brought this over brought it a very, very long way, and I thank them for their service. Again, I can't remember what I was doing, but I remember being in enough of a rush that I couldn't stop to ask the driver what their whole deal was — something I'd otherwise do — and it's a regret I'll live with forever.

Anyway, that's enough for me. How about you all drop on down below and share your weirdest non-USDM car spotting moments? I'll be handing out bonus points to folks who can provide photographic evidence of their findings, Big Year birding-style.

The U.S. is getting just 700 Heritage Edition cars, all of them decked out in a color the company is calling Blazing Phoenix Yellow. It's not the same paint code as the old Type R of yore, but Acura says it's a brighter and more saturated replacement.

The Heritage Edition is just a cosmetic package, there's no power upgrades or trick suspension here, but it does go deeper than just the yellow paint. The car also gets blacked-out badges, a titanium shift knob, and copper wheels — all from Acura's existing accessory catalog, but bundled together for this model. Each car is also done up with a black interior, which includes yellow accent stitching that matches the Heritage Edition's exterior. (That yellow stitching is found on any 2027 Integra Type S with the black interior, not just this special edition.)

The rest of the Integra Type S' changes for 2027 aren't huge — gloss black mirror caps and wheels, yellow brake calipers, and a mirror that automatically tilts down when you back up aren't exactly game-changing upgrades — but there's not much that can be done to improve on the Integra's existing state. Blazing Phoenix Yellow is enough, and I truly hope that these cars aren't all snatched up by investors to be squirreled away in climate-controlled garages. Let these things drive, let them breathe like the DC2 Integras by which they're inspired. I want to see these out on the roads.

article_paragraphs: Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at l ower-than-believable prices . But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features . The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example…
The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023 :

The M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.
One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those big brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.

My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

Daimler-Benz deserves kudos for being one of the few stalwart automakers to still sell a traditional estate model here in the U.S. Mercedes has offered a wagon on the E-Class platform for nearly half a century, beginning with the W123 in 1977. Yesterday, we looked at that model's prodigy of nearly two decades later (and with only one major model change): a 1995 Mercedes-Benz E320 Estate .

That car came to us in stately silver, with the promise of proper maintenance and no mechanical issues. It also had all the wagon-y goodness one could want, with a spacious load area and a fold-up rear-facing third row to take us all back to our formative years. That was all enough to make the classic Benz a solid contender at its $10,250 asking price. We all circled our wagons and awarded the longroof a razor-thin 51% 'Nice Price' win.

Yesterday's Mercedes held a lot of appeal, with its classic proportions, legendary build quality, and status-symbol three-pointed star hood ornament. What if, however, you needed something similar, but with vastly more room inside, more pedestrian mechanicals to make maintenance easier, and a price tag that eschewed any sense of status-seeking? If those criteria fit your expectations and budget (more on that in a minute), then the 1999 Ford Expedition XLT 4X4 we have under adjudication today should fit the bill.

Ford introduced the Expedition for the 1997 model year, basing it on the then-new F-Series pickup chassis and styling it to look like the company's wildly popular, and more fun-sized Explorer. Nominally, the Expedition replaced the long-in-the-tooth two-door Bronco in Ford's sales-leading truck lineup. Sorry, O.J. It also finally gave Ford a direct competitor to Chevrolet's long-running Suburban three-row SUV, something the company had never offered before.

The mad mix of solid F-Series stoutness and Explorer-curious-buyer-friendly style proved a winning combination for the Expedition, and even more so for the Lincoln Navigator that it spawned, the model that arguably has kept the lights on at Ford's fancy-pants brand for more than three decades.

This Expedition comes in appliance white over an institutional but dutifully long-wearing gray mousefur-and-plastic interior. There's nothing particularly fancy or luxurious about this large SUV, which is laudable for anyone seeking basic but dang-big transportation. And dang-big it is.

If you were buying Fords at Costco, this would be the model the box stores would offer, and you'd probably have to buy two of them, connected by a plastic grab handle. The deets are: a 119-inch wheelbase, supporting over 200 inches of overall length. With over six and a half feet of overall width, the truck offers more than 63 inches of interior shoulder room for stretching out or for road trip games of slug bug.

title: Honda Previews All-New CR-V As It Transitions To 100% Hybrid Power
raw_summary: America’s best-selling SUV is getting a lighter platform, a next-gen hybrid system, and a sharper new look. Honda has confirmed that the next-generation CR-V will arrive next year and be sold exclusively as a hybrid. It will bolster the brand's efforts to compete with the Toyota RAV4 , which is also sold solely as a hybrid in the U.S. The compact crossover will also be the first Honda to launch with its latest-generation two-motor hybrid system.
summary: America’s best-selling SUV is getting a lighter platform, a next-gen hybrid system, and a sharper new look. Honda has confirmed that the next-generation CR-V will arrive next year and be sold exclusively as a hybrid. It will bolster the brand's efforts to compete with the Toyota RAV4 , which is also sold solely as a hybrid in the U.S.
article_paragraphs: America’s best-selling SUV is getting a lighter platform, a next-gen hybrid system, and a sharper new look.

Honda has confirmed that the next-generation CR-V will arrive next year and be sold exclusively as a hybrid. It will bolster the brand's efforts to compete with the Toyota RAV4 , which is also sold solely as a hybrid in the U.S. The compact crossover will also be the first Honda to launch with its latest-generation two-motor hybrid system.

The Japanese marque has teased the new CR-V with a single image showing the updated badge. Dealers who were recently shown the next-gen CR-V at a retailer meeting in Las Vegas said the new model will include thin LED headlights, a full-width LED light signature at the rear, and "muscular rear haunches," Auto News reports. While we will have to wait a little longer to see the new CR-V in person, Honda has already published several important details about its platform and powertrain.

Underpinning the SUV will be Honda's all-new mid-size architecture that was announced 12 months ago. A new structure and engineering methods have allowed Honda to save 198 lbs (90 kg) from its current hybrid platform, and Honda wants more than 60% of parts to be shared between the models built on it, which should help cut costs.

The platform has been developed to be more rigid in some areas and less rigid in others than the current architecture, allowing for more flex during cornering to "realize an unprecedented level of driving stability and a sporty and pleasant driving experience." The platform will also incorporate Honda's new Motion Management System to control posture and the same advanced pitch control technology as the Accord and Prelude.

Honda's new hybrid system also promises to be an improvement on the outgoing system. Known simply as the Honda Hybrid, this powertrain will drive 15 next-generation hybrid models launching by March 31, 2030. The hybrid will include a new 2.0-liter Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder with direct injection and a pair of updated electric motors. The manufacturer claims the next-gen Honda Hybrid system will cost 30% less to produce than the current hybrids and improve fuel economy by over 10%. The new CR-V will also be equipped with Honda's latest electric all-wheel-drive system.

"With a 100% hybrid powertrain, the next-generation Honda CR-V will further expand the appeal of America's most popular SUV as demand for hybrid-electric vehicles reaches record levels," Luis Guerra, assistant vice president of Honda National Auto Sales, said in a statement. The current CR-V is on track to surpass 400,000 sales for the third consecutive year.

Honda has confirmed the new CR-V will be built at its factories in Ohio, Indiana, and Canada. Its new Honda Hybrid powertrain will also be manufactured at the Honda Transmission Plant in Ohio , while the new four-cylinder engine will be built at the Anna Engine Plant, Honda's largest auto engine plant anywhere.

title: New Hero Street Fighter Bike Spied Testing - Electric Vida UBX?
raw_summary: Hero MotoCorp has been working on expanding their premium motorcycle and scooter business with multiple new launches. However, the company is also busy with expanding their Vida portfolio. Currently, we have the V2 family and then VX2 family of electric scooters. Along with that, we also have Vida Dirt.E K3 electric dirt bike for kids. Now, Hero wants to get into the mainstream electric motorcycle segment and the company has showcased VXZ Concept (Vida X Zero) and then the Ubex Concept. The latter seems to have commenced testing in the country and the latest spy shots of Hero Vida UBX looks like it is production-ready, if not, close to being production-ready.

article_paragraphs: Hero MotoCorp has been working on expanding their premium motorcycle and scooter business with multiple new launches. However, the company is also busy with expanding their Vida portfolio. Currently, we have the V2 family and then VX2 family of electric scooters. Along with that, we also have Vida Dirt.E K3 electric dirt bike for kids.

Now, Hero wants to get into the mainstream electric motorcycle segment and the company has showcased VXZ Concept (Vida X Zero) and then the Ubex Concept. The latter seems to have commenced testing in the country and the latest spy shots of Hero Vida UBX looks like it is production-ready, if not, close to being production-ready.

At the 2025 EICMA Show in Milan, Hero MotoCorp showcased the VXZ and UBX concept electric bikes and a year later in 2026 EICMA Show, the company showcased prototypes of these. While the latest spy shots are not clear and leave for some speculations whether it is VXZ or UBX, the wheel design leans towards this being UBX than VXZ.

There were two riders on this motorcycle which masked quite a lot of the motorcycle to match the proportions. Also, making it difficult to pin point it, was the heavy camouflage. Overall aesthetics suggest that it is a Hero Vida electric motorcycle, but the straight wheel spokes nudges it towards being the UBX.

The bike gets sporty street bike appeal and it is likely to appeal to young buyers. At the front, we can see a single LED projector headlight and sleek LED indicators. We can also see the instrument cluster that also doubles up as a faux flyscreen.

Hero Vida UBX prototype was recently revealed at EICMA 2026 and the latest spy shot looks like it gets similar equipment. For starters, the production-spec model is likely to retain USD telescopic front forks and rear mono-shock suspension setup. Also, front and rear disc brakes. Battery pack would be positioned where the engine would normally go.

And on Vida UBX prototype, we can also see some protective bodywork that looks quite nice. Single-piece seat with a rear step, all-LED lighting, mid-mounted electric motor and fancy swingarm could also be retained from the unveiled prototype. There’s also a beak like structure below headlights which could make it to production.

Keyhole might be on the tank area and switchgear could be fancy-type to control the TFT instrument cluster. Prototype had massive rear tyre hugger and chain drive and something similar could be seen on production-spec vehicle too.

raw_title: Denza D9 and Z9 GT Launched In India, Priced From Rs. 90 Lakh
title: Denza D9 and Z9 GT Launched In India, Priced From Rs. 90 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Both models imported as CBUs from China and offered with a complimentary 11 kW home charger and a standard 6-year/1,50,000 km warranty Denza, one of BYD Auto’s several car brands, has launched the D9 and Z9 GT as its first cars in India. The company offers both models in plug-in hybrid and pure electric variants internationally but has brought only the latter to India. The D9 costs Rs. 90 lakh (ex-showroom), while the Z9 GT retails at Rs. 1.57 crore (ex-showroom). The Denza D9 is a premium MPV like the MG M9, measuring 5,250 mm in length, 1,960 mm in width, and 1,900 mm in height, along with a 3,110-mm wheelbase. It accommodates seven people with a 2+2+3 seating layout. The front seats are 8-way electrically adjustable and offer 4-way power lumbar support, massage, memory, ventilation, and heating functions. Front occupants also get two 50-watt wireless charging pads. The second-row seats are captain’s chairs featuring 10-way power adjustment, electrically adjustable leg rests, 10-point massage, memory, ventilation, and heating. Second-row passengers also get two cup holders and a hot and cold refrigerator, both integrated into the rear of the centre console, as well as two 50-watt wireless charging pads. The third-row seats are 4-way electrically adjustable. A front-mounted electric motor produces 340 kW (456 hp) and 365 Nm of torque, and it uses electricity stored in a 115.07 kWh LFP battery pack. This setup allows the D9 to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 8.5 seconds and travel up to 730 kilometres, as per NEDC. Charging from 10% to 97% SoC takes just 9 minutes via BYD’s new Flash Chargers, although this infrastructure does not exist in our market at the moment. The Denza Z9 GT is a full-size shooting brake, measuring 5,180 mm in length, 1,990 mm in width, and 1,490 mm in height, along with a 3,125 mm wheelbase. It offers 495 liters of luggage space, which can be expanded to 1,680 litres by folding the rear seat. It comes with features like a dual-chamber air suspension, rear-wheel steering, pencil compass turn, crab-walk mode, and a retractable tail wing. Inside, the driver and front passenger get 8-way electrically adjustable seats with 4-way power lumbar support, massage, memory, ventilation, and heating functions, powered headrests, and 2-way power thigh support. The rear seat is 2-way power adjustable and offers massage, power recline, ventilation, and heating functions. Other interior highlights include a 13.2-inch 2.5K front passenger screen, a 20-speaker Devialet sound system, a hot and cold refrigerator, two 50-watt front wireless charging pads in the front, and a 50-watt rear wireless charging pad in the rear. The Z9 GT sports three electric motors, including two 310 kW (416 hp)/400 Nm units in the back and a 230 kW (308 hp)/410 Nm unit in the front, powered by a 122.49 kWh LFP battery pack. With 850 kW (1,140 hp) of total power and 1,210 Nm of total torque, the car accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in just 2.7 seconds and reaches a top speed of 270 km/h. It can travel up to 670 kilometres on a single charge, as per NEDC. The 122.49 kWh LFP battery pack also takes only 9 minutes to charge from 10% to 97% SoC, but only with BYD’s new Flash Chargers, which are not available in India.
